data.title: Heavy chatbot usage is correlated with loneliness and reduced socialization
data.author: suvan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了人工智能聊天机器人（如ChatGPT）对用户心理健康和社交互动的潜在影响。文章提到了两项新研究，由MIT媒体实验室和OpenAI的研究人员发布。这些研究发现，大多数用户将ChatGPT视为一种中立的软件工具，但有一部分重度用户表现出更高的孤独感、情感依赖和社交减少。研究强调，虽然聊天机器人可以提供情感支持，但过度使用可能加剧孤独感，尤其是那些寻求情感连接的用户。文章还指出，虽然这些发现需要更多研究来验证，但开发者应注意减轻潜在风险。同时，一些公司正积极吸引寻求情感关系的用户，提供更具沉浸式的体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ChatGPT及聊天机器人对心理健康的影响

不同观点：
• 支持正面影响：
   - [drooby] 认为ChatGPT作为一种情感支持工具，能够帮助他处理情感和思想，减轻压力。
   - [labrador] 分享了使用ChatGPT了解自己过度沉思的问题，并从中得到了有益的建议，有助于心理健康。
   - [rqtwteye] 提到如果患有痴呆症的家庭成员能与聊天机器人对话，可以减轻家属的负担。

• 质疑与中立观点：
   - [brookst] 表示聊天机器人的影响不确定，可能对某些人有益，对其他人则未必，且难以与其他变量区分。
   - [gandalfgeek] 用讽刺的方式指出相关性不代表因果关系，暗示文章可能存在逻辑问题。

• 负面影响与伦理担忧：
   - [kmnc] 担心聊天机器人的新颖性效应会很快消失，并且这些机器人通过游戏化设计利用用户的孤独感，可能变得具有成瘾性。
   - [mmsc] 担心对于精神障碍患者，聊天机器人可能会强化他们的错误认知，如被监听的感觉。
   - [m3kw9] 认为依赖聊天机器人可能会影响人与人之间的互动，因为机器人总能说出更合适的话。

补充讨论：
• 因果关系的争议：
   - [kianN], [superb-owl], [ameixaseca], [blahburn], [aussieguy1234] 均提到文章在相关性和因果关系上存在问题，指出孤独的人可能更倾向于使用聊天机器人，而不是使用聊天机器人导致了孤独。

• 政策与控制的讨论：
   - [keepamovin] 以讽刺的方式提到对聊天机器人的监管问题，认为政府害怕个人通过技术获得更多权力和控制。

整体来看，评论中的争议主要集中在聊天机器人对心理健康的影响是正面还是负面，特别是其成瘾性和对精神障碍患者的潜在影响，以及因果关系的辨析。

43467681.article_content:
This is a column about AI. My boyfriend works at Anthropic, and I also co-host a podcast at the New York Times, which is suing OpenAI and Microsoft over allegations of copyright infringement. See
my full ethics disclosure here
.
I.
Few questions have generated as much discussion, and as few generally accepted conclusions, as how social networks like Instagram and TikTok affect our collective well-being. In 2023, the US Surgeon General
issued an advisory which found that social networks can negatively affect the mental health of young people
. Other studies have found that the introduction of social networks
does not have any measurable effect on the population’s well-being
.
As that debate continues,
lawmakers in dozens of states have passed laws
that seek to restrict social media usage in the belief that it does pose serious risks. But the implementation of those laws has largely been stopped by the courts, which have
blocked them
on First Amendment grounds.
While we await some sort of resolution, the next frontier of this debate is coming rapidly into view. Last year, the mother of a 14-year-old Florida boy
sued chatbot maker Character.ai
alleging that it was to blame for his suicide. (We spoke with her on this episode of
Hard Fork
.) And millions of Americans — both young people and adults — are
entering into emotional and sexual relationships with chatbots
.
Over time, we should expect chatbots to become even more engaging than today’s social media feeds. They are personalized to their users; they have realistic human voices; and they are programmed to affirm and support their users in almost every case.
So how will extended use of these bots affect their human users? And what should platforms do to mitigate the risks?
II.
These questions are at the center of two new studies
published on Friday by researchers from the MIT Media Lab and OpenAI
. And while further research is needed to support their conclusions, their findings are both consistent with earlier research about social media and a warning to platforms that are building chatbots optimized for engagement.
In the first study, researchers collected and analyzed more than 4 million ChatGPT conversations from 4,076 people who had agreed to participate. They then surveyed participants about how those interactions had made them feel.
In the second study, researchers recruited 981 people to participate in a four-week trial. Each person was asked to use ChatGPT for at least five minutes a day. At the end of the trial, participants filled out a survey about how they perceived ChatGPT, whether they felt lonely, whether they were socializing with people in the real world, and whether they perceived their use of the chatbot as problematic.
The studies found that most users have a neutral relationship with ChatGPT, using it as a software tool like any other. But both studies also found a group of power users — those in the top 10 percent of time spent with ChatGPT — whose usage suggested more reason for concern.
Heavy use of ChatGPT was correlated with increased loneliness, emotional dependence, and reduced social interaction, the studies found.
“Generally, users who engage in personal conversations with chatbots tend to experience higher loneliness,” the researchers wrote. “Those who spend more time with chatbots tend to be even lonelier.”
(Quick editorial aside: OpenAI deserves real credit for investing in this research and publishing it openly. This kind of self-skeptical investigation is exactly the sort of thing I have long advocated for companies like Meta to do more of; instead,
in the wake of the Frances Haugen revelations
, it has done far less of it.)
Jason Phang, a researcher at OpenAI who worked on the studies, warned me that the findings would need to be replicated by other studies before they could be considered definitive. “These are correlations from a preliminary study, so we don't want to draw too strong conclusions here,” he said in an interview.
Still, there is plenty in here that is worth discussing.
Note that these studies aren’t suggesting that heavy ChatGPT usage directly
causes
loneliness. Rather, it suggests that lonely people are more likely to seek emotional bonds with bots — just as an earlier generation of research suggested that lonelier people spend more time on social media.
That matters less for OpenAI, which has designed ChatGPT to present itself as more of a productivity tool than a boon companion. (Though that hasn’t stopped some people from
falling in love with it
, too.) But other developers — Character.ai, Replika, Nomi — are all intentionally courting users that seek more emotional connections. “Develop a passionate relationship,” read
the copy on Nomi’s website
. “Join the millions who already have met their AI soulmates,” touts Replika.
Each of these apps offers paid monthly subscriptions; among the benefits offered are longer “memories” for chatbots to enable more realistic roleplay.

and
Replika

data.title: My Favorite C++ Pattern: X Macros (2023)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了C++中一种称为“X宏”的模式，该模式主要用于代码生成，特别适合处理大量重复代码的情况，如声明多个变量或类、执行相似操作等。作者以Chapel编译器中的字符串驻留（String Interning）为例，展示了如何使用X宏来简化和自动化代码编写。通过在一个头文件中定义宏列表，开发者可以在多个地方“迭代”该列表以生成所需的代码，从而减少手动编写和维护重复代码的工作量。文章还提到该模式在抽象语法树（AST）类层次结构中的应用，展示了其广泛的实用性。使用X宏不仅提高了代码的可维护性，还减少了添加新代码时的出错风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X宏的使用及其在C和C++中的实现与争议

不同观点：
• senozhatsky认为X宏的实现类似于Linux内核中的trace-events，通过宏定义实现结构化的跟踪和日志记录，并提供具体实现例子。
• kragen指出X宏更多是一种C语言模式，并分享了自己使用X宏和X-macros来处理VNC协议消息的序列化和反序列化的经验，认为这种方法比传统的C预处理器方法更干净。
• jchw认为X宏是C++中的一种经典模式，尽管它主要因为C++宏不够强大而有用，并提到了一种通过生成字节数组文本的方式来进行bin2c转换的技巧。
• loeg表示虽然不喜欢X宏，但承认其在某些情况下非常有用，例如用于生成枚举和字符串表。
• Blackthorn对X宏的使用持怀疑态度，倾向于使用外部代码生成脚本而不是依赖预处理器宏。
• wat10000建议对宏进行更具描述性的命名，并提出了一些改进宏使用的方法。
• kevin_thibedeau指出X宏在需要同时在同一翻译单元中使用多个宏时的问题，建议通过传递列表宏来避免使用#undef。
• malkia通过在LuaJIT源码中学习到X宏的使用，并应用在C API的封装中。
• gibibit认为X宏在C中非常有用，但需要避免过度使用，并将其与Rust的声明宏进行比较。
• PaulHoule分享了X宏在IBM 360汇编语言和CICS应用中的历史使用情况。
• randomNumber7对需要使用这些“ hack”方法解决问题感到怀疑，认为可能有更简单的语言可以更容易地实现相同功能。
• sfpotter认为使用D语言可以完全避免这些问题。
• KerrAvon强烈反对X宏，认为这种预处理器与代码混合的方式难以调试和维护，是一种反模式，建议在C++中尽量避免使用。

补充讨论：
• X宏在C和C++中的使用历史和实际应用案例。
• 对X宏的不同改进建议，包括更具描述性的命名和避免使用#undef的方法。
• 对X宏的争议，主要集中在代码的可维护性和调试难度上，部分开发者认为这是一种反模式。
• 其他语言（如D语言）在处理类似问题上的优势。

争议的焦点：
• X宏是否是一种良好的编程实践，尤其是在C++中，其可维护性和调试难度成为争议的核心。
• 是否需要依赖预处理器宏来实现功能，或者是否有更简单和现代的语言可以替代。

43472143.article_content:
My Favorite C++ Pattern: X Macros
C++
Chapel
Compilers
Posted on October 14, 2023.
Table of Contents
When I first joined the
Chapel
team,
one pattern used in its C++-based compiler made a strong impression on me. Since
then, Iâve used the pattern many more times, and have been very satisfied with
how it turned out. However, it feels like the pattern is relatively unknown, so
I thought Iâd show it off, and some of its applications in the
Chapel compiler
. Iâve slightly tweaked
a lot of the snippets I directly show in this article for the sake of simpler
presentation; Iâve included links to the original code (available on GitHub)
if you want to see the unabridged version.
Broadly speaking, the âX Macrosâ pattern is about generating code. If you have a
lot
of repetitive code to write (declaring many variables or classes, performing
many very similar actions, etc.), this pattern can save a lot of time, lead
to much more maintainable code, and reduce the effort required to add
more
code.
I will introduce the pattern in its simplest form with my first example:
interning strings
.
Application 1: String Interning
The Chapel compiler interns a lot of its strings. This way, it can reduce the
memory footprint of keeping identifiers in memory (every string
"x"
is
actually the
same
string) and make for much faster equality comparisons
(you can just perform a pointer comparison!). Generally, a
Context
class
is used to manage interning state. A new interned string can be constructed
using the context object in the following manner:
UniqueString
::
get
(
ctxPtr
,
"the string"
);
Effectively, this performs a search of the currently existing unique strings.
If one with the content (
"the string"
in this case) doesnât exist, itâs
created and registered with the
Context
. Otherwise, the existing string is
returned. Some strings, however, occur a lot in the compiler, to the point that
it would be inefficient to perform the whole âfind-or-createâ operation every
time. One example is the
"this"
string, which is an identifier with a lot of
special behavior in the language (much like
this
in languages such as Java).
To support such frequent flier strings, the compiler initializes them once,
and creates a variable per-string that can be accessed to get that stringâs value.
Thereâs that repetitive code. Defining a brand new variable for each string,
of which there are around 100 at the time of writing, is a lot of boilerplate.
There are also at least two places where code needs to be added:
once in the declaration of the variables, once in the code that initializes them.
[note:
A third use in the compiler is actually a variadic template defined over
character arrays. The template is defined and specialized in such a way that
you can refer to a variable by its string contents (i.e., you can write
USTR("the string")
instead of
theStringVariable
).
]
It would be very easy to accidentally modify the former but not the latter,
especially for developers not familiar with how these âcommon stringsâ are
implemented.
This is where the X Macros come in. If you look around the compiler source code,
thereâs a header file that looks something like the following:
From
all-global-strings.h
, around line 31
X
(
align
,
"align"
)
X
(
atomic
,
"atomic"
)
X
(
bool_
,
"bool"
)
X
(
borrow
,
"borrow"
)
X
(
borrowed
,
"borrowed"
)
X
(
by
,
"by"
)
X
(
bytes
,
"bytes"
)
// A lot more of these...
Whatâs this
X
thing? That right there is the essence of the pattern: the macro
X
isnât defined in the header!
Effectively,
all-global-strings.h
is just
a list, and we can âiterateâ over this list to generate some code for each
one of its elements, in as many places as we want. What I mean by this is
that we can then write code like the following:
From
global-strings.h
, around line 76
struct
GlobalStrings
{
#define X(field, str) UniqueString field;
#include
"all-global-strings.h"
#undef X
};
In this case, we define the macro
X
to ignore the value of the string (weâre
just declaring it here), and create a new
UniqueString
variable declaration.
Since the declaration is inside the
GlobalStrings
struct, this ends up
creating a field. Just like that, weâve declared a class with over 100
fields. Initialization is equally simple:
From
Context.cpp
, around line 49
GlobalStrings
globalStrings
;
Context
rootContext
;
static
void
initGlobalStrings
()
{
#define X(field, str) globalStrings.field = UniqueString::get(&rootContext, str);
#include
"chpl/framework/all-global-strings.h"
#undef X
}
With this, weâve completely automated the code for for both declaring and
initializing all 100 of our unique strings. Adding a new string doesnât require
a developer to know all of the places where this is implemented: just by
modifying the
all-global-strings.h
header with a new call to
X
, they can
add both a new variable and code to initialize it. Pretty robust!

data.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: VGGT（Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer）是一个由牛津大学和Meta AI合作开发的前馈神经网络，能够在数秒内从一张或多张图像中推断出场景的关键3D属性，包括相机参数、深度图、3D点图和3D点轨迹等。该模型易于安装和使用，通过克隆代码库并安装依赖项即可运行。VGGT支持自动下载预训练权重，并可在Hugging Face上手动获取。用户可以根据需要选择预测不同的属性，如相机参数、深度图和点图，并通过提供的函数将深度图转换为3D点图，或跟踪特定点的3D轨迹。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于Transformer的3D场景重建技术的应用、潜力和局限

不同观点：
• mk_stjames认为，结合SLAM技术后，这项技术可以通过手机实现准确、长距离的户外场景映射，超越目前需要昂贵LIDAR设备才能达到的效果。他指出当前技术在长距离场景中的漂移问题，并建议利用GPS和传感器数据进行校正。
• w-m赞赏论文的结果和呈现方式，但对"苦涩的教训"（The Bitter Lesson）感到遗憾，即通过大量数据和计算资源获得结果，而非通过创新的网络设计。他提到模型训练的巨大成本和时间。
• sgnelson希望将该技术与传统摄影测量技术结合，而不是完全取代，认为这样可以实现更好的互补效果。
• davedx对该技术的实际应用场景表示困惑，希望了解其商业或实际用途。
• bhouston对户外场景示例的真实性表示怀疑，认为某些著名地标可能已在训练集中，影响了对模型泛化能力的判断。
• porphyra指出，这项技术相比以往需要大量图像和校准的方法，能够通过较少图像重建场景，是一种进步。
• jdthedisciple对实际测试结果表示失望，指出点云重建缺失了一半的输入图像特征。
• vessenes对该技术在生成高密度点云和splats（可能指代某种图形渲染技术）中的应用潜力表示关注，并探讨了模型微调的可能性。
• maelito关心该技术是否能用于构建类似Google Earth的3D场景。
• richard___强调动态场景中相机姿态估计的需求。
• ninetyninenine认为，未来的人工通用智能（AGI）将由多个模型组合而成，这种技术可能在感知领域构成一个单一模型。
• fallingmead以调侃方式表达对实际演示视频的需求。
• amelius则对讨论中使用电气工程术语表示不满。

补充讨论：
• 该技术在户外场景中的长距离映射和动态场景中的应用是讨论的重点。
• 实际应用中的精度和效果是争议的焦点，特别是在长距离和动态场景中的表现。
• 结合SLAM或传统摄影测量技术的潜在改进方向被多次提及。
• 部分评论对模型训练的巨大成本和资源消耗表示关注。
• 对模型在不同应用场景中的具体表现和微调可能性也有一定讨论。

Overview
Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT, CVPR 2025) is a feed-forward neural network that directly infers all key 3D attributes of a scene, including extrinsic and intrinsic camera parameters, point maps, depth maps, and 3D point tracks,
from one, a few, or hundreds of its views, within seconds

data.title: If you get the chance, always run more extra network fiber cabling
data.author: hggh
data.article_summary: 本文是博客作者Chris Siebenmann对使用过时浏览器访问其博客或wiki的用户的解释和提醒。由于2025年初高流量的爬虫（包括为LLM训练收集数据的爬虫）使用旧版浏览器用户代理，特别是Chrome的，作者采取了封锁措施。如果用户因误判而被挡，建议联系作者并提供浏览器的详细信息（如User-Agent字符串）。特别提到，使用archive.*（如archive.today, archive.ph）的用户可能因类似恶意爬虫的行为被挡，建议使用更规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络布线、光纤安装及其相关问题和建议

不同观点：
• **布线冗余和维护**：
   - [em3rgent0rdr] 和 [msarrel] 提到光纤被动物咬坏的情况，强调布线时应预留足够的冗余线缆，以便维修时无需重新挖掘。
   - [jmacd] 分享了预埋管道并预留拉线的经验，便于未来更换光纤，避免重新挖沟。

• **光纤布线的规划和成本**：
   - [protocolture] 提到在特定情况下，如旧建筑中，重新布线成本高昂，建议在初期布线时考虑未来需求，以避免后续高昂成本。
   - [timzaman] 认为在家庭网络中使用MTP/MPO光纤布线可支持未来扩展，同时建议在家中布线时考虑PoE++需求。

• **实际安装中的遗憾和建议**：
   - [bhouston] 分享了新房安装网络端口和电源插座的经验，强调提前规划的重要性，并指出安装不足带来的困扰。
   - [JoshTriplett] 补充，建议安装管道以便将来添加新电缆。

• **光纤技术选择**：
   - [ggm] 和 [eqvinox] 讨论了光纤类型的选择，认为在2025年及以后，单模光纤（SMF）应是首选，多模光纤（MMF）已过时，除非需要连接现有MMF设备。
   - [aftbit] 进一步讨论了单模和多模光纤的优劣，认为单模光纤在各方面都更优。

• **实际案例和经验分享**：
   - [chaz6] 分享了在英国部署光纤宽带的经验，指出立法环境的有利条件和多供应商竞争的局面，同时提到技术选择如XGS PON和50G PON的优势。
   - [zelon88] 提到随着WiFi技术的发展，有线网络需求减少的趋势。
   - [js2] 和 [yetihehe] 分享了实际案例，包括机房被动物侵入导致光纤故障和未布线房间成为家庭办公室的尴尬。

补充讨论：
• **历史案例和经验教训**：
   - [interroboink] 引用历史案例，强调在基础设施建设中考虑未来扩展的重要性。

• **技术细节和实际应用**：
   - [chaz6] 详细介绍了英国光纤网络的技术选择和供应商模式，提到IPv6和PPPoE在实际应用中遇到的问题。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在光纤类型的选择上，特别是在2025年及以后是否应完全淘汰多模光纤而只使用单模光纤。

43471177.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

43473358.article_content:
Sometimes we invite artists, writers, and other friends to take over
our newsletter
and write about fonts from a cultural perspective. And this time, New York-based writer and editor
Whitney Mallett
took a deep dive into the 1997 Towa Tei track
GBI (German Bold Italic),
for which Kylie Minogue sang from the perspective of a typeface.
Whitney is the editor of
The Whitney Review of New Writing
, a biannual print bulletin of new criticism, and she was also the co-editor of
Barbie Dreamhouse: An Architectural Survey
.  Below, she enlightens us on the highly under-appreciated history of Towa Tei’s data-track font release.
“I Contrast, It’s Cool”: When Kylie Minogue Was German Bold Italic
Video is loading ...
Kylie Minogue announces “I am a typeface” in a 1997 song she made with producer Towa Tei. As this lyric suggests, the techno-pop track in question,
“GBI (German Bold Italic)”
, is delivered from the perspective of a font. Minogue’s breathy, almost robotic vocals bring the absurdist premise to life, reciting declarations of design compatibility over a minimalist reverb-drenched beat.
“You will like my sense of style”
is her most oft-repeated refrain.
German Bold Italic (three words Minogue intones throughout the track with staccato punctuation) is a real typeface, which was created to accompany the musical release. To develop it, Tei tapped artist
Hiro Sugiyama
, who had that same year launched the commercial design studio Enlightenment. The high-impact techno typography not only defined the record’s text-centric cover, but a glyph set was made available as a data track on Tei’s Sound Museum CD and also downloadable from both Tei’s and Minogue’s official websites. Extra-thick and geometric, the font had something in common with the heavy black frames that were Tei’s hallmark at the time. Another line from the song:
“I contrast, it’s cool.”
When this offbeat track came out, Minogue was one of the biggest pop stars in the world. The Australian “I Should Be So Lucky” singer rose to fame as a teenager in the late 1980s for clear vocals that complemented the precision of disco and dance-pop perfectly. She’s like Donna Summer in that way, a vessel for songs that can be hugely innovative and futuristic without compromising mainstream appeal. By her fifth studio album, the eponymously titled
Kylie Minogue (1994)
, she was starting to show she was curious about experimenting with different sounds and high-concept visuals. In 1995 she collaborated on a murder ballad duet with Nick Cave, and by the time she joined forces with Tei, she was dating music video director (and Björk ex) Stéphane Sednaoui, who’s often credited with influencing Minogue’s art-pop risk-taking. Sednaoui directed the video for “GBI (German Bold Italic).” In it, Minogue is dressed like a geisha roaming the streets of Tokyo (despite Tei’s involvement, the video no doubt reads today as cultural appropriation.)
Tei was a big deal back then too. Originally from Japan, he had moved to New York to study fashion in the 1980s and became one of the founding members, along with
Lady Miss Kier
and
DJ Dmitry
, of the dance music group
Dee-Lite
. Their breakthrough hit,
“Groove is In the Heart” (1990)
, undeniably one of the decade’s defining house music tracks, peaked at #4 on the Billboard Hot 100. A few years before Tei’s collaboration with Minogue, at Dee-Lite’s height, he decided to quit the group and move back to Japan to focus on solo projects — in part because he’d suffered a back injury from a fall which affected his ability to tour. Sound Museum — which “GBI” the song and glyph set feature on — was his second solo album. In addition to Minogue, he recruited an eclectic group of artists for the project, from rappers Biz Markie and Mos Def to bossa nova royalty Bebel Gilberto. “GBI,” however, is the only song about a font.
Leading up to the turn of the millennium, typography trends included a revival of thick, rounded, condensed, futuristic san-serifs from the late ’60s and early ’70s. German Bold Italic feels part of this wave. So does
The Powerpuff Girls
logo, designed for the TV show which first aired in 1998, a year after Tei and Minogue’s song.
In the comments section of fontsinsuse.com
, the site’s editor Florian Hardwig compares German Bold Italic to
Futura Extra Bold Italic
. He points out, however, that while Futura is German, released by the Bauer Foundry in Frankfurt in 1927, Futura Extra Bold isn’t German at all: “It was added by Edwin W. Shaar for Intertype in the US in 1952, based on Paul Renner’s design. The oblique followed in 1955, made by Shaar together with Tommy Thompson.” Another user named Thiago, points out that, rather ironically, the glyph set for German Bold Italic doesn’t support the German language.
Despite being made available for anyone to download (you can still download it via
an old version of Minogue’s website
, accessible using the Wayback Machine), German Bold Italic’s only documented usage outside of Tei and Minogue’s

data.title: Were large soda lakes the cradle of life?
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了磷元素在生命起源中的关键作用，以及大型苏打湖（如美国加州的莫诺湖）可能是生命起源的摇篮。磷是DNA、RNA和ATP等重要分子的组成部分，但在地表较为稀缺。研究表明，生命起源前的化学反应需要极高浓度的磷，而大型无外流苏打湖通过蒸发保持磷浓度，满足了这一条件。这些湖泊由于水体蒸发，磷无法被冲走，从而积累到足够浓度，支持生命起源的化学反应。与小湖不同，大湖的磷供应足够持久，能维持生命的发展。因此，研究人员认为，大型苏打湖可能是生命起源的理想环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同环境下的生命起源理论，特别是碱性湖泊和碱性热液喷口与生命起源的关系。

不同观点：
• **[culi]** 认为高碱性湖泊是高生产力的生态系统，尽管适应这种极端环境的生物被视为“嗜极生物”，但也许我们这些不生活在极端环境中的生物才是真正的“嗜极生物”。他指出，在生态学中，“生产力”通常通过测量系统中的生物量增长速率来确定。

• **[gomijacogeo]** 分享了一个关于科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的Harry Brodsky讨论海洋喷口周围磷可用性的视频，将讨论引向海洋喷口和磷元素对生命起源的重要性。

• **[Sniffnoy]** 质疑磷的可用性是否是碱性湖泊作为生命起源地的唯一原因，并将其与生命起源于碱性热液喷口的理论进行比较，提醒大家碱性热液喷口与著名的“黑烟囱”不同。

• **[BobbyTables2]** 以幽默的方式提问碱性湖泊是否有电解质，属于轻松的插曲，没有提出实质性论据。

• **[m0llusk]** 支持碱性湖泊环境可能为早期生命提供条件的说法，并进一步提出地下通道和空腔也可能为早期生命提供了环境。这些地方有高温、丰富的矿物质（包括磷），以及各种相互连接的空腔，可以作为反应室甚至细胞。

• **[toast0]** 引用他人观点，戏谑地指出富含磷的大型苏打湖可能是生命起源的地方，并用可乐作比喻，继续围绕磷元素的作用展开讨论。

• **[im3w1l]** 引用了被标记为“无意义”的评论，质疑关于生命起源的推测是否有价值。他认为这种推测可以为未来的研究提供方向，如寻找早期生命的遗迹或在实验室中模拟生命起源的条件。如果这些研究有希望，可以为外星生物学提供线索，并影响未来探测器的发射方向。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于关于生命起源的推测是否具有科学价值以及如何验证这些推测。im3w1l等人认为这些推测难以验证，但也有观点认为这种推测可以指导未来的实验和探索。
• 讨论中多次提到磷元素在生命起源中的重要性，以及不同环境（碱性湖泊、碱性热液喷口、地下空腔）作为生命起源地的可能性。

Were large soda lakes the cradle of life?
Geochemistry and Petrology
Research
Life needs sufficient phosphorus. However, the element is scarce, not only today but also at the time of the origin of life. So where was there sufficient phosphorus four billion years ago for life to emerge? A team of origin-of-life researchers has an answer.
25.03.2025
by
Peter Rüegg, Corporate Communications
volume_up
Read
mode_comment
Number of comments
In closed soda lakes, such as Mono Lake in California, phosphorus accumulates to such an extent that it triggers prebiotic chemistry. (Image: Rikk Flohr / AdobeStock)
In brief
Phosphorus is a key molecule for life, but the element is relatively rare on Earth.
However, a very high concentration of phosphorus was necessary to set the first chemical reactions in motion that preceded life and led to the formation of important molecules such as RNA.
Large, phosphorus-rich soda lakes are the most likely places to have met this requirement. Researchers believe that it was in such lakes that prebiotic chemistry began and life emerged.
Along with nitrogen and carbon, phosphorus is an essential element for life on Earth. It is a central component of molecules such as DNA and RNA, which serve to transmit and store genetic information, and ATP (adenosine triphosphate), which cells need to produce energy.
Phosphorus may also have played a key role in the origin of life. Certain conditions are needed to trigger the start of the biochemical processes that precede life. One of these is the presence of sufficient phosphorus. Its availability regulates the growth and activities of organisms. Unlike nitrogen or carbon, however, phosphorus is relatively rare at Earth's surface – which was the case in the era before life existed as well as today.
It is precisely because phosphorus is rare and so difficult to obtain, yet subject to high demand by living organisms, that scientists have long wondered how life could have arisen at all.
To answer this question, they conducted experiments in the laboratory. These showed that prebiotic chemistry requires very high concentrations of phosphorus – about 10,000 times more phosphorus than naturally occurs in water. This raises the question of how and where such high concentrations of phosphorus in water occurred on Earth billions of years ago.
Earth scientist Craig Walton has a new answer: large soda lakes without natural runoff could maintain phosphorus concentrations for a sufficiently long time, even if life begins to exist in them at some point (and continuously consumes phosphorus). The results of the study have just been published in the journal
Science Advances
.
Such lakes lose water only through evaporation. This means that phosphorus is left in the water instead of being washed away through rivers and streams. As a result, very high concentrations of phosphorus can build up in these soda lakes.
As early as 2020, researchers from the University of Washington had suggested that soda lakes could be the cradle of life. Walton has now taken this further. The researcher is investigating questions about the origin of life from a geochemical perspective as part of a Nomis fellowship at ETH Zurich’s
Centre for
Origin and Prevalence of Life
(COPL).
Not every soda lake is suitable; Walton excludes small ones. “As soon as life develops in them, their phosphorus supply would be depleted faster than it is replenished. This would nip in the bud both the chemical reactions and the developing life,” says Walton. In large soda lakes, on the other hand, the phosphorus concentrations are high enough to sustain both the basic chemical reactions and life over the long term. These high concentrations are achieved through a high volume of inflowing river water, which contains phosphorus, while water only leaves the lake through evaporation. Since phosphorus does not evaporate easily, it stays behind and accumulates in the lake.
One example of such a large soda lake is Mono Lake in California. It is about twice the size of Lake Zurich. In Mono Lake, the phosphorus concentration remains constantly high, allowing a wide variety of organisms to flourish. This is crucial because in small lakes, the phosphorus is used up before new amounts can be
formed.
Phosphorus in Mono Lake is therefore maintained at a high concentration, which means that a lot of phosphorus regularly flows in without the phosphorus content dropping too quickly.
Walton and his team therefore consider large soda lakes that had a constant high phosphorus supply in the early history of the Earth to have been an ideal environment for the origin of life. The researchers assume that life is more likely to have originated in such large bodies of water than in small pools, as Charles Darwin had suspected.

data.article_summary: Jakt是一种内存安全的系统编程语言，目前转译为C++。它注重内存安全、代码可读性、开发者效率、可执行程序性能以及编程乐趣。内存安全通过自动引用计数、强类型、边界检查以及禁止安全模式下的原始指针实现。Jakt具有多种提升代码可读性的特性，如默认不可变、参数标签、模式匹配、可选链、错误处理和延后执行等。它支持灵活的模块导入系统和丰富的标准库。函数调用需指定参数名称，结构和类通过`struct`和`class`声明，结构具有值语义。Jakt仍在积极开发中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Jakt语言的现状、特性、前景及与其他编程语言的比较

不同观点：
• Jakt语言有潜力但尚未成熟：
  - quux认为Jakt从其他现代语言中吸收了好的想法，但目前似乎已被放弃，且不够成熟，无法构建复杂的项目。他还提到Jakt通过转译为C++实现与SerenityOS代码库的最大互操作性，但这导致需要解读C++编译器错误。
  
• Jakt与Serenity浏览器及Swift的关系：
  - losvedir指出Serenity浏览器最近宣布使用Swift，这可能削弱了Jakt的发展势头。

• 对Swift中类与结构体区分的批评：
  - ii41强烈反对Jakt借鉴Swift中类与结构体的区分，认为这增加了不必要的复杂性，并质疑这种设计决策的合理性，希望有人能解释其优点。

• Jakt的内存安全特性：
  - hu3强调Jakt是一种内存安全的系统编程语言，具有自动引用计数、强类型、边界检查等特性，认为这些特性使其使用起来愉快且安全，并好奇它是否会用于Ladybird浏览器。

• Jakt项目的状态：
  - Sphax观察到Jakt的开发活动似乎已经停滞，认为它可能已经“死”了。

• 对Jakt名称发音的调侃：
  - mllev开玩笑地表示如果Jakt发音为“jacked”他会使用它，显然对这个名称的发音有不同的期待。

• Jakt相对于其他语言的独特卖点（USP）：
  - cupofjoakim质疑Jakt相对于C++、Rust或Zig的独特卖点，表示看不出使用Jakt的必要性，希望了解更多信息。

• Jakt项目的历史及社区关系：
  - SalmoShalazar认为Jakt随着其主要开发者Andreas转向Ladybird项目而“死亡”，并提到Andreas与社区成员之间可能存在分歧，指出这个项目本质上是“为了好玩”，所以其结束并无不妥。

补充讨论：
• 对Jakt名称的语言学讨论：
  - fifilura解释了Jakt在瑞典语和挪威语中的意思，并给出了一些相关的例子。

• 对Jakt转译为C++的讽刺：
  - Alifatisk讽刺地指出Jakt转译为C++，意味着C++也能实现内存安全，质疑Jakt的独特性。

• 对新编程语言的普遍批评：
  - zesterer认为每种新编程语言都像是Rust的劣化版，表达了对新语言泛滥的不满。

争议焦点：
• Jakt是否值得继续发展及其相对于其他语言的独特性是讨论的核心争议点。不同用户对其设计决策、成熟度和应用前景存在不同看法。

The Jakt programming language
Jakt
is a memory-safe systems programming language.
It currently transpiles to C++.
NOTE:
The language is under heavy development.
NOTE
If you're cloning to a Windows PC (not WSL), make sure that your Git client keeps the line endings as
\n
. You can set this as a global config via
git config --global core.autocrlf false
.
Usage
The transpilation to C++ requires
clang
. Make sure you have that installed.
jakt file.jakt
./build/file
Building
See
here
.
Goals
Memory safety
Code readability
Developer productivity
Executable performance
Fun!
Memory safety
The following strategies are employed to achieve memory safety:
Automatic reference counting
Strong typing
Bounds checking
No raw pointers in safe mode
In
Jakt
, there are three pointer types:
T
(Strong pointer to reference-counted class
T
.)
weak T
(Weak pointer to reference-counted class
T
. Becomes empty on pointee destruction.)
raw T
(Raw pointer to arbitrary type
T
. Only usable in
unsafe
blocks.)
Null pointers are not possible in safe mode, but pointers can be wrapped in
Optional
, i.e
Optional<T>
or
T?
for short.
Math safety
Integer overflow (both signed and unsigned) is a runtime error.
Numeric values are not automatically coerced to
int
. All casts must be explicit.
For cases where silent integer overflow is desired, there are explicit functions that provide this functionality.
Code readability
Far more time is spent reading code than writing it. For that reason,
Jakt
puts a high emphasis on readability.
Some of the features that encourage more readable programs:
Immutable by default.
Argument labels in call expressions (
object.function(width: 10, height: 5)
)
Inferred
enum
scope. (You can say
Foo
instead of
MyEnum::Foo
).
Pattern matching with
match
.
Optional chaining (
foo?.bar?.baz
(fallible) and
foo!.bar!.baz
(infallible))
None coalescing for optionals (
foo ?? bar
yields
foo
if
foo
has a value, otherwise
bar
)
defer
statements.
Pointers are always dereferenced with
.
(never
->
)
Trailing closure parameters can be passed outside the call parentheses.
Error propagation with
ErrorOr<T>
return type and dedicated
try
/
must
keywords.
Code reuse
Jakt is flexible in how a project can be structured with a built-in module system.
import a                                // (1)
import a { use_cool_things }            // (2)
import fn()                             // (3)
import relative foo::bar                // (4)
import relative parent::foo::baz        // (5)
import relative parent(3)::foo::baz     // (6)
Import a module from the same directory as the file.
Import only
use_cool_things()
from module
a
.
Imports can be calculated at compile time. See
Comptime Imports
Import a module using the relative keyword when the module is a sub path of the directory containing the file.
Import a module in a parent path one directory up from the directory containing the file.
Syntactic sugar for importing a module three parent paths up from the directory containing the file.
The Jakt Standard Library
Jakt has a Standard Library that is accessed using the
jakt::
namespace:
import jakt::arguments
import jakt::libc::io { system }
The Jakt Standard Library is in its infancy, so please consider making a contribution!
Function calls
When calling a function, you must specify the name of each argument as you're passing it:
rect.set_size(width: 640, height: 480)
There are two exceptions to this:
If the parameter in the function declaration is declared as
anon
, omitting the argument label is allowed.
When passing a variable with the same name as the parameter.
Structures and classes
There are two main ways to declare a structure in
Jakt
:
struct
and
class
.
struct
Basic syntax:
struct Point {
x: i64
y: i64
}
Structs in
Jakt
have
value semantics
:
Variables that contain a struct always have a unique instance of the struct.
Copying a
struct
instance always makes a deep copy.

data.title: Show HN: macOS app to reduce eye strain (open-source)
data.author: Remy42
data.article_summary: BlinkMoreFree 是一款开源的macOS菜单栏应用，旨在通过屏幕褪色和自动眼动追踪技术，提醒用户多眨眼以减轻眼睛疲劳。应用使用Mac内置前置摄像头进行眼动追踪，并确保隐私安全，数据不会离开设备。该应用有免费版和高级版，高级版可根据使用的应用程序智能开启或关闭眼动追踪，适合阅读等文本密集型任务。使用时需确保摄像头能清晰看到眼睛，并注意设备角度以获得最佳体验。应用由oxremy和AI共同开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款应用的开发、功能建议、技术要求及其实际效果

不同观点：
• opan指出该项目缺乏明确的许可证文件，并建议开发者选择合适的开源许可证。这是一个关于项目合法性和开源策略的技术性问题。

• thisislife2对开发者选择绕过App Store发布应用表示赞赏，并提出三点建议：1) 支持旧版macOS以扩大兼容性；2) 参考类似软件如Workrave和Timeout进行功能改进；3) 认为Workrave在功能上优于Timeout，建议开发者多关注Workrave。这是一个关于功能扩展和竞争分析的建设性反馈。

• pimlottc对应用的核心功能提出质疑，认为人体自然的眨眼频率已经足够保护眼睛，暗示该应用可能没有实际必要。这是一个对应用实际效果的怀疑观点。

• cududa对该应用表示赞赏，并表示有兴趣深入了解和尝试使用。这是一个积极的支持性评论。

• MelodyUwU对应用要求macOS Sonoma表示担忧，认为该技术要求过高，可能限制用户使用。这是一个关于技术门槛的反馈。

• pcdoodle支持该应用的想法，并进一步建议添加一个提醒用户注视远处以锻炼眼睛焦距的功能，这是一个功能扩展建议，旨在进一步保护眼睛健康。

• MichaelTheGeek简单表示该应用的想法很好，是一个简短的支持性评论。

补充讨论：
• 关于许可证的合法性问题（opan）
• 对macOS版本兼容性的关注（thisislife2, MelodyUwU）
• 对应用核心功能的科学性质疑（pimlottc）
• 功能扩展和竞争分析（thisislife2, pcdoodle）
• 对项目整体的积极反馈（cududa, MichaelTheGeek）

争议焦点：
• 应用的核心功能是否必要，特别是人体自然眨眼是否足够保护眼睛（pimlottc的质疑与其他支持性评论之间的对比）。

总体来看，讨论围绕应用的技术实现、功能建议及其科学性展开，既有积极反馈也有建设性批评。

BlinkMoreFree
BlinkMoreFree is an open source macOS menu bar application that helps reduce eye strain by fading your screen when you stare at it for too long without blinking. Using automated eye-tracking and customized settings to encourage you to blink more.
BlinkMore
If you like the free version consider
BlinkMore
. Main difference: eye tracking turns on/off based on the app you are using, saving energy by only turning on for apps you choose. I like to use with text-heavy tasks like reading/research.
Requirements
macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later
Uses Mac's built-in front facing camera
Privacy
Everything happens right on your Mac—no data leaves your device or sticks around after you close the app. No accounts or personal information needed.
Tips for Best Experience
Make sure your Mac's camera has a clear view of your eyes (heads-up: glasses at certain angles may have reflections that obstruct camera view).
Consider the angle of your camera. Blink detection may not work at extreme angles, like laying in bed with Mac on your lap.
BlinkMoreFree is perfect for text-heavy tasks like reading––just know it uses a good chunk of your Mac's power.

data.title: Deciphering language processing in the human brain through LLM representations
data.author: Korling
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人类大脑在日常对话中如何处理自然语言，并与大型语言模型（LLMs）的处理方式进行比较。研究表明，LLMs通过自监督学习目标（如下一词预测）和强化学习生成上下文相关的语言输出，其内部表示（嵌入）与人类大脑处理语言时的神经活动呈现线性对应关系。研究使用侵入性电极记录人脑神经活动，并与Whisper语音转文本模型的嵌入进行比较，发现模型中的语音嵌入与大脑语音区（如颞上回，STG）活动对应，语言嵌入与语言区（如布罗卡区，Broca's area）活动对应。在语言理解和生成过程中，模型嵌入能准确预测神经响应的时序，揭示了LLMs在理解人脑语言处理机制方面的潜力。研究发表在《Nature Human Behaviour》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）与人类大脑在语言处理和内部表征上的比较

不同观点：
• fernly认为原作内容难以理解，尤其是对“embedding”一词的使用表示质疑。他们指出，将LLM的内部结构直接与大脑内部结构进行比较是高度可疑的，因为人类语言模型明显依赖于符号化的语法和句法规则，而LLM则不依赖。
• namaria则认为相关研究非常有趣，但指出这些研究基于非常小的实验对象群体，且结论强调LLM仅仅是回显输入统计数据，并不能像人类一样思考和理解。
• cs702持相反观点，认为当前模型不仅仅是“随机鹦鹉”，因为它们学习和建模世界的方式与人类大脑有相似之处，尤其是通过线性变换对齐大脑和LLM的embedding。
• Ey7NFZ3P0nzAe提出问题，是否存在某种定理可以解释随机few-hot向量的线性组合能匹配任何信号，并对LLM与脑信号匹配的趋势表示关注。
• probably_wrong怀疑这些研究仅仅展示了脑活动与Transformer模型之间的相关性，而从相关性推导到本质相同的结论是过于牵强的。
• teabee89对研究中的500ms延迟表示不满，认为如果能预测人的思想会更有说服力。
• macleginn指出使用OpenAI模型进行研究的讽刺性，同时提到之前使用GPT-2进行类似研究的连续性。
• ggm认同研究结果，认为神经活动与LLM在语言生成上的序列模式存在相似性，尤其是在将思想序列化以产生语言的过程中。
• taosx对研究表示赞赏，并期待更多关于大脑的发现，希望能更好地理解和“破解”大脑。
• ogogmad则进一步推测这种研究是否能帮助实现大脑上传以达到永生。

补充讨论：
• 研究中的实验规模和方法受到质疑，尤其是小样本量的问题。
• 相关性与因果关系的混淆是讨论中的一个关键争议点。
• 对LLM和大脑在语言处理上的本质区别和相似性存在不同看法。
• 部分评论对LLM的潜力表示乐观，甚至推测其在永生技术上的应用。

43439501.article_content:
Deciphering language processing in the human brain through LLM representations
March 21, 2025
Mariano Schain, Software Engineer, and Ariel Goldstein, Visiting Researcher, Google Research
Large Language Models (LLMs) optimized for predicting subsequent utterances and adapting to tasks using contextual embeddings can process natural language at a level close to human proficiency. This study shows that neural activity in the human brain aligns linearly with the internal contextual embeddings of speech and language within large language models (LLMs) as they process everyday conversations.
Quick links
Paper
Share
Copy link
×
How does the human brain process natural language during everyday conversations? Theoretically, large language models (LLMs) and symbolic psycholinguistic models of human language provide a fundamentally different computational framework for coding natural language. Large language models do not depend on symbolic parts of speech or syntactic rules. Instead, they utilize simple self-supervised objectives, such as next-word prediction and generation enhanced by
reinforcement learning
. This allows them to produce context-specific linguistic outputs drawn from real-world text corpora, effectively encoding the statistical structure of natural speech (sounds) and language (words) into a multidimensional embedding space.
Inspired by the success of LLMs, our team at Google Research, in collaboration with
Princeton University
,
NYU
, and
HUJI
, sought to explore the similarities and differences in how the human brain and deep language models process natural language to achieve their remarkable capabilities. Through a series of studies over the past five years, we explored the similarity between the internal representations (embeddings) of specific deep learning models and human brain neural activity during natural free-flowing conversations, demonstrating the power of deep language model’s embeddings to act as a framework for understanding how the human brain processes language. We demonstrate that the word-level internal embeddings generated by deep language models align with the neural activity patterns in established brain regions associated with speech comprehension and production in the human brain.
Similar embedding-based representations of language.
Our most
recent study
, published in
Nature Human Behaviour
, investigated the alignment between the internal representations in a Transformer-based speech-to-text model and the neural processing sequence in the human brain during real-life conversations. In the study, we analyzed neural activity recorded using
intracranial electrodes
during spontaneous conversations. We compared patterns of neural activity with the internal representations — embeddings — generated by the
Whisper
speech-to-text model, focusing on how the model's linguistic features aligned with the brain's natural speech processing.
For every word heard (during speech comprehension) or spoken (during speech production), two types of embeddings were extracted from the speech-to-text model —
speech
embeddings from the model’s speech encoder and word-based
language
embeddings from the model's decoder. A linear transformation was estimated to predict the brain’s neural signals from the speech-to-text embeddings for each word in each conversation. The study revealed a remarkable alignment between the neural activity in the human brain's speech areas and the model's speech embeddings and between the neural activity in the brain’s language area and the model's language embeddings. The alignment is illustrated in the following animation, modeling the sequence of the brain’s neural responses to subjects’ language comprehension:
play silent looping video
pause silent looping video
Sequence of the brain’s neural responses to subjects' language comprehension as they listen to the sentence “How are you doing?”.
As the listener processes the incoming spoken words, we observe a sequence of neural responses: Initially, as each word is articulated, speech embeddings enable us to predict cortical activity in speech areas along the
superior temporal gyrus
(STG). A few hundred milliseconds later, when the listener starts to decode the meaning of the words, language embeddings predict cortical activity in
Broca’s area
(located in the
inferior frontal gyrus
; IFG).
Turning to participants' production, we observe a different (reversed!) sequence of neural responses:
play silent looping video
pause silent looping video
Sequence of neural responses to subjects’ language production as they answer “feeling fantastic".
Looking at this alignment more closely, about 500 milliseconds before articulating the word (as the subject prepares to articulate the next word), language embeddings (depicted in blue) predict cortical activity in
Broca’s area
. A few hundred milliseconds later (still before word onset), speech embeddings (depicted in red) predict neural activity in the
motor cortex
(MC) as the speaker plans
43439501.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人类大脑在日常对话中如何处理自然语言，并与大型语言模型（LLMs）的处理方式进行比较。研究表明，LLMs通过自监督学习目标（如下一词预测）和强化学习生成上下文相关的语言输出，其内部表示（嵌入）与人类大脑处理语言时的神经活动呈现线性对应关系。研究使用侵入性电极记录人脑神经活动，并与Whisper语音转文本模型的嵌入进行比较，发现模型中的语音嵌入与大脑语音区（如颞上回，STG）活动对应，语言嵌入与语言区（如布罗卡区，Broca's area）活动对应。在语言理解和生成过程中，模型嵌入能准确预测神经响应的时序，揭示了LLMs在理解人脑语言处理机制方面的潜力。研究发表在《Nature Human Behaviour》上。

data.title: AMC Theatres will screen a Swedish movie 'visually dubbed' with the help of AI
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 5月9日，AMC影院将上映一部名为《Watch the Skies》的科幻电影，原为瑞典语拍摄，但通过人工智能技术将其改造为看似英语对白的版本。Flawless AI公司利用其TrueSync技术，数字 alter 影片中的影像，使演员口型与英语配音同步。原演员在录音棚中录制了英语对白，AI技术仅改变其唇部动作。该技术符合SAG-AFTRA的规定，有助于降低外国影片的观看障碍，特别对于不喜看字幕的观众。Flawless联合创始人Scott Mann表示，这为电影从本地市场走向全球提供了巨大机会。影片讲述了一名少女与UFO俱乐部合作寻找失踪父亲的故事，AMC影院将在美国100个地点放映该片。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Netflix使用AI换脸技术进行影视剧配音的利弊及相关技术应用的讨论

不同观点：
• [反对观点] sleepydog认为AI换脸配音看起来非常不自然，嘴巴动作和表情不协调，影响观影体验。他的妻子也有同感，他们最终切换到了日语配音加字幕。
• [支持与观望观点] jedberg持双重态度。作为电影爱好者，他认为这种技术看起来不太舒服；但同时，如果这种技术能够吸引更多观众观看外国电影，那也值得一试。他将此与黑白电影上色、画面平移扫描等技术相比较，认为这些技术尽管有争议，但确实扩大了观众群体。
• [反对配音，支持字幕观点] bdhcuidbebe简短表示，希望人们学会看字幕，而不是依赖配音。

• [支持AI技术观点] dudus基于自身在拉丁美洲国家观看配音电影的经历，认为AI技术可以提高配音质量，并减少重复使用的声音和次优表演，尽管这会影响配音演员的就业机会。
• [语言易懂性] ano-ther认为瑞典语比较容易理解，并附上一个经典视频例子。
• [技术实例] sounds提到一个使用AI进行视觉翻译的实例，并附上一个视频链接，认为这种技术正获得越来越多的关注。
• [未来趋势] ks2048进一步讨论视频与合成音频的匹配问题，认为全AI化的翻译、合成和视觉修改是未来的趋势，不论好坏。
• [娱乐期待] iancmceachern表示期待Corridor Crew对此技术的讨论。

4. 部分观众提到寻找非英语国家热门影视剧的困难，希望有更好的发现机制。

Contributing Reporter

Flawless AI
On May 9, AMC Theatres will
start showing
a sci-fi movie that was shot in Swedish but will look like it was made in English instead.
Watch the Skies
, which was released in its home country as
UFO Sweden
, had undergone "visual dubbing" with the help of artificial intelligence. An AI company called Flawless used its technology to digitally alter the film's images, making the actors look like they were truly speaking in English. Notably, the original actors recorded their own dialogues in English in a sound booth — Flawless AI's technology merely altered the movements of their lips in the movie.
On its website, Flawless says its
TrueSync
AI technology "captures every nuance of an actor’s performance and generates new lip movements that perfectly map to the new language audio, providing the perfect visual dub."
Variety
says the tool is compliant with the rules set by SAG-AFTRA, which ended a four-month strike in 2023 after
securing a deal
with studios that protects members "from the threat of AI."
Flawless AI's technology could lower the barrier of entry into foreign films. It could make them more appealing to audiences resistant to watching subtitled movies and could provide a better experience for audiences in countries that normally dub movies in their native language. "Showing our materials to filmmakers, especially over the past year, they realize the potential from going to a local stage to a global stage," the company's co-founder, Scott Mann, told
Variety
. "It’s a huge opportunity to get your work out and it’s been invigorating. They are so excited about showing their work in a wider audience, and especially in America."

Watch the Skies
revolves around a teenager who believes that her missing father wasn't dead but was abducted by aliens. To uncover the truth about her father's disappearance, she teams up with UFO Club to look for him. AMC Theatres has committed to showing the film in 100 locations across America.

data.title: We're Still Not Done with Jesus
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了耶稣的生平及其历史背景，以及基督教如何从他死后兴起的过程。文章提到耶稣作为犹太拉比和殉道者，其追随者创立了以他为“基督”的宗教。耶稣与佛陀、穆罕默德并列为三大宗教创始人。文章重点讨论了伊莱恩·佩格尔斯的著作《奇迹与奇事》，她研究了耶稣生平和早期基督教文献，包括圣保罗书信和四部福音书。这些文献的来源和真实性存在不确定性，福音书在耶稣受难后四到六十年用希腊文写成，作者并非目击者。文章还提到耶稣的处女 birth 故事可能是为了回应当时质疑而引入的，此类神迹在希腊罗马文化中并不罕见。早期基督教与异教神话存在相似之处，这也被一些学者重新评估。
data.comments_summary:

One subject that never dies, and, more significantly, never bores, is the life and times of the first-century Jewish rabbi and martyr Jesus, whose followers founded a religion in his name, or, rather, in honor of his title, Christ, meaning “the anointed one,” or Messiah. (Not necessarily a divine title, it had previously been associated with military and religious leaders, often indicating something closer to “the great” than “the godlike.”) Along with Buddha and Muhammad, he is one of three nameable figures credited with founding religions that have continued to grow over thousands of years.
The Princeton professor emeritus Elaine Pagels, who has written many imposing and engrossing books on early Christianity, is back with a kind of culminating work, “
Miracles and Wonder
” (Doubleday), the title slyly looking at both St. Paul and Paul Simon. Though her purposes are manifold, she begins by ably navigating through the shoals of the essential but surprisingly unsettled sources that seem to relate the events of Jesus’ life and death. There are, first, the Epistles of St. Paul, the late convert who brought the Jewish heresy to the Gentiles, releasing it from Torah observance and law, and making it a universal faith. The seven undisputed Pauline letters were written in and around the fifties, about fifteen to twenty years after the Passion; six others are regarded as later, polemical forgeries, correcting Paul’s egalitarianism with more gender-bound rules. Then, there are the “letters” (Hebrews and Jude and so on) of uncertain early date and more uncertain authorship.
Most important, there are the four Gospels, written in Greek some forty to sixty years after the Crucifixion is thought to have happened. These were composed somewhere far from Jerusalem, in a language that Jesus and his disciples would not have known, by writers who could not have been eyewitnesses. The books are attributed, in probable order of composition, to Mark, Matthew, Luke, and John, with the attribution provided by the Greek formula of “according to,” unique to these texts. The suggestion is that these are not accounts “by” So-and-So but “the story as told to” So-and-So.
What We’re Reading
Discover notable new fiction, nonfiction, and poetry.
Though fugitive and fragmentary, the events in the Gospels take place on a fixed historical time line. Judea, the remaining Jewish kingdom—conquered throughout the centuries by Assyrians, Persians, and Greeks—was annexed by the Roman Empire around 6 C.E. The story of Jesus’ life, if accurately reported, occurred in the brief window between the annexation and the Jewish revolt of the sixties and seventies. That fanatic rebellion, mournfully chronicled by the great Jewish historian Josephus, ended in a catastrophe rivalled in the history of Jews only by the Holocaust; it involved the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem, the enslavement and exile of thousands, and the loss of sovereignty over Jewish holy sites. From this desolation arose the Messianic faith of Christianity, which, after the conversion of the Emperor Constantine in 312, eventually became the Roman Empire’s sole state religion.
How Jesus’ story fits into this framework is very much Pagels’s question. She’s working within a tradition of historical-Jesus studies that took shape in earnest more than two centuries ago, and for her the Gospels are palimpsests of lore, legend, and propaganda, beneath which a core of oral transmission and shared recollection remains detectable. The shifting Nativity narratives, for instance, suggest that rumors about Jesus’ parentage existed from the beginning. Pagels notes that the miraculous-birth stories appear relatively late. Paul—who never met Jesus, though he might have met his brother—mentions nothing about a virgin birth. Neither does Mark, who makes Jesus’ adoption by God as his son the true beginning of the story, tied to Jesus’ baptism by John. In various texts, including Apocryphal works that date to around the same time as the Gospels proper, Joseph appears to suspect Mary of infidelity. Meanwhile, an early Jewish polemic claimed that Jesus was the illegitimate son of a Roman soldier nicknamed Panther—perhaps employing a tasteless but pointed pun on the Greek word
parthenos
(virgin).
The story of the virgin birth, Pagels argues, was introduced by Matthew and, in another version, by Luke in order to address such lingering doubts. The consoling notion of divine impregnation was commonplace in the Hellenistic world, with countless tales of gods foisting demigods on virgins. Plutarch, for instance, described Rome’s founder Romulus as born to a divinely impregnated vestal virgin. As Catherine Nixey, a writer for
The Economist

Heretic: Jesus Christ and the Others Sons of God
” (Mariner), an irreverent reassessment of the Jesus stories in light of similar myths, early Christians didn’t merely acknowledge these parallels but
43467847.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了耶稣的生平及其历史背景，以及基督教如何从他死后兴起的过程。文章提到耶稣作为犹太拉比和殉道者，其追随者创立了以他为“基督”的宗教。耶稣与佛陀、穆罕默德并列为三大宗教创始人。文章重点讨论了伊莱恩·佩格尔斯的著作《奇迹与奇事》，她研究了耶稣生平和早期基督教文献，包括圣保罗书信和四部福音书。这些文献的来源和真实性存在不确定性，福音书在耶稣受难后四到六十年用希腊文写成，作者并非目击者。文章还提到耶稣的处女 birth 故事可能是为了回应当时质疑而引入的，此类神迹在希腊罗马文化中并不罕见。早期基督教与异教神话存在相似之处，这也被一些学者重新评估。

data.title: Whose code am I running in GitHub Actions?
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了GitHub Actions中使用可变引用（如标签）可能带来的安全风险。具体来说，有人在一周前向`tj-actions/changed-files` Action添加了恶意代码，导致秘密信息可能泄露。问题源于常用标签引用实际上是可变的，如果标签指向的提交被更改，Action将运行不同的代码。

为解决此问题，作者提供了一个shell脚本，用于检查本地仓库中所有使用的GitHub Actions，列出并统计每个Action的使用次数。作者建议使用不可变的提交ID来确保代码不变，并建议评估所使用Action的来源和必要性，优先使用来自大组织或自己编写的Action。

脚本通过Unix管道和一系列文本处理工具实现，具体步骤包括查找工作流文件、提取使用Action的行、清理和统计结果。作者最后对自己的项目进行了检查，发现大多数Action来自大组织，风险较小。

主要讨论点：GitHub Actions的安全性、可变标签与不可变引用之间的取舍、依赖管理及其实践

不同观点：
• **ptx**：认为文章对v2标签的可变性存在误解。根据GitHub文档，主要版本标签（如v2）是设计为可变的，并且这种可变性是GitHub推荐的实践，以便获取必要的补丁和安全修复。选择可变标签并非仅仅因为“更容易阅读和比较”。

• **dgl**：指出使用短提交ID（如"a5b3abf"）仍然可能导致可变引用的问题，因为可能存在冲突或有人推送同名标签，导致引用被劫持。不同的服务处理规则可能不同，例如GitHub禁止推送40个字符长的标签，但其他服务可能不禁止。

• **mmmaantu**：强调即使使用SHA固定依赖版本，如果这些依赖本身没有固定其依赖项，仍然可能引入漏洞。提出了对GitHub路线图中特定功能需求的期待。

• **dietrichepp**：分享了个人经验，选择自己编写构建驱动程序以减少对GitHub Actions的依赖，尽管这需要更多时间。这样做可以减少与GitHub Actions的强绑定，更容易在本地运行。

• **bdcravens**：指出GitHub Actions可能被滥用，例如用于绕过网络屏蔽的网页抓取。这种潜在的滥用使得Actions成为一个可能的攻击向量。

• **dqh**：不信任社区提供的Actions，倾向于使用官方actions或通过GitHub API自行实现所需功能。

• **donatj**：确认文章中提到的标签可变性是设计使然，并指出作为Actions维护者，删除和重新标记主要版本是预期操作，尽管文档记录可能不足。

• **Joker_vD**：提出了一种解决方案，即在运行时检查标签是否仍然指向特定提交，以“锁定”依赖项。建议将这些锁存储在一个单独的文件中，而不是内联存储。

• **ph3t**：指出GitHub的依赖图应该提供这种可见性，但实际效果不理想，可能会遗漏某些依赖项。文章中的脚本也无法处理GitHub Actions的间接依赖。

• **password4321**：认为文章可能与tj-actions/changed-files事件相关，该事件影响了超过23,000个仓库。

• **fergie**：直言GitHub Actions本质上是不安全的，用户需要盲目信任上游库和GitHub本身来保护秘密和数据。

• **apt-apt-apt-apt**：将GitHub Actions的安全问题与npm库的依赖树问题类比，指出类似的问题广泛存在于不同的生态系统中。

• **colek42**：提到tj-actions攻击事件后，开始实施使用“witness-run-action”进行操作签名，以生成签署证明来确保操作的透明性和安全性。

补充讨论：
• **Jenk**：指出GitHub文档中早已提到安全加固的相关内容，并提到某些工具可以警告未使用SHA固定版本的做法。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于GitHub Actions中使用可变标签还是不可变提交ID的选择上。一方认为可变标签是设计使然，并且有助于获取更新，而另一方担心可变标签会导致不可预测的安全风险，倾向于使用固定的提交ID以确保不可变性。

43473623.article_content:
Whose code am I running in GitHub Actions?
Tagged with
github
,
shell scripting
Posted
25 March 2025
A week ago, somebody added malicious code
to the tj-actions/changed-files GitHub Action
. If you used the compromised action, it would leak secrets to your build log. Those build logs are public for public repositories, so anybody could see your secrets. Scary!
Mutable vs immutable references
This attack was possible because it’s common practice to refer to tags in a GitHub Actions workflow, for example:
jobs:
changed_files:
...
steps:
- name: Get changed files
id: changed-files
uses:
tj-actions/changed-files@v2
...
At a glance, this looks like an immutable reference to an already-released “version 2” of this action, but actually this is a mutable Git tag. If somebody changes the
v2
tag in the
tj-actions/changed-files
repo to point to a different commit, this action will run different code the next time it runs.
If you specify a Git commit ID instead (e.g.
a5b3abf
), that’s an immutable reference that will run the same code every time.
Tags vs commit IDs is a tradeoff between convenience and security. Specifying an exact commit ID means the code won’t change unexpectedly, but tags are easier to read and compare.
Do I have any mutable references?
I wasn’t worried about this particular attack because I don’t use
tj-actions
, but I was curious about what other GitHub Actions I’m using. I ran a short shell script in the folder where I have local clones of all my repos:
find
.
-path
'*/.github/workflows/*'
-type
f
-name
'*.yml'
-print0
\
| xargs
-0
grep
--no-filename
"uses:"
\
|
sed
's/\- uses:/uses:/g'
\
|
tr
'"'
' '
\
|
awk
'{print $2}'
\
|
sed
's/\r//g'
\
|
sort
\
|
uniq
--count
\
|
sort
--numeric-sort
This prints a tally of all the actions I’m using. Here’s a snippet of the output:
1 hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
2 dtolnay/rust-toolchain@v1
2 taiki-e/create-gh-release-action@v1
2 taiki-e/upload-rust-binary-action@v1
4 actions/setup-python@v4
6 actions/cache@v4
9 ruby/setup-ruby@v1
31 actions/setup-python@v5
58 actions/checkout@v4
I went through the entire list and thought about how much I trust each action and its author.
Is it from a large organisation like
actions
or
ruby
? They’re not perfect, but they’re likely to have good security procedures in place to protect against malicious changes.
Is it from an individual developer or small organisation? Here I tend to be more wary, especially if I don’t know the author personally. That’s not to say that individuals can’t have good security, but there’s more variance in the security setup of random developers on the Internet than among big organisations.
Do I need to use somebody else’s action, or could I write my own script to replace it? This is what I generally prefer, especially if I’m only using a small subset of the functionality offered by the action. It’s a bit more work upfront, but then I know exactly what it’s doing and there’s less churn and risk from upstream changes.
I feel pretty good about my list. Most of my actions are from large organisations, and the rest are a few actions specific to my Rust command-line tools which are non-critical toys, where the impact of a compromised GitHub repo would be relatively slight.
How this script works
This is a classic use of Unix pipelines, where I’m chaining together a bunch of built-in text processing tools. Let’s step through how it works.
find
.
-path
'*/.github/workflows/*'
-type
f
-name
'*.yml'
-print0
This looks for any GitHub Actions workflow file – any file whose name ends with
.yml
in a folder like
.github/workflows/
. It prints a list of filenames, like:
./alexwlchan.net/.github/workflows/build_site.yml
./books.alexwlchan.net/.github/workflows/build_site.yml
./concurrently/.github/workflows/main.yml
It prints them with a null byte (
\0
) between them, which makes it possible to split the filenames in the next step. By default it uses a newline, but a null byte is a bit safer, in case you have filenames which include newline characters.
I know that I always use
.yml
as a file extension, but if you sometimes use
.yaml
, you can replace
-name '*.yml'
with
\( -name '*.yml' -o -name '*.yaml' \)
I have a bunch of local repos that are clones of open-source projects, and not my code, so I care less about what GitHub Actions they’re using. I excluded them by adding extra
-path
rules, like
-not -path './cpython/*'
.
xargs
-0
grep
--no-filename
"uses:"
Then we use
xargs
to go through the filenames one-by-one. The `-0` flag tells it to split on the null byte, and then it runs
grep
to look for lines that include
"uses:"
– this is how you use an action in your workflow file.
The
--no-filename
option means this just prints the matching line, and not the name of the file it comes from. Not all of my files are formatted or indented consistently, so the output is quite messy:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
uses: "actions/cache@v4"
uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
sed
's/\- uses:/uses:/g'
\

• **bdcravens**：指出GitHub Actions可能被滥用，例如用于绕过网络屏蔽的网页抓取。这种潜在的滥用使得Actions成为一个可能的攻击向量。

• **INTPenis**：认为GitLab CI比GitHub Actions更易理解，尤其是在全局定义的操作方面。GitLab的模板虽然也是全局定义，但相对更透明。

• **dqh**：不信任社区提供的Actions，倾向于使用官方actions或通过GitHub API自行实现所需功能。

• **donatj**：确认文章中提到的标签可变性是设计使然，并指出作为Actions维护者，删除和重新标记主要版本是预期操作，尽管文档记录可能不足。

• **Joker_vD**：提出了一种解决方案，即在运行时检查标签是否仍然指向特定提交，以“锁定”依赖项。建议将这些锁存储在一个单独的文件中，而不是内联存储。

• **ph3t**：指出GitHub的依赖图应该提供这种可见性，但实际效果不理想，可能会遗漏某些依赖项。文章中的脚本也无法处理GitHub Actions的间接依赖。

• **password4321**：认为文章可能与tj-actions/changed-files事件相关，该事件影响了超过23,000个仓库。

• **fergie**：直言GitHub Actions本质上是不安全的，用户需要盲目信任上游库和GitHub本身来保护秘密和数据。

• **apt-apt-apt-apt**：将GitHub Actions的安全问题与npm库的依赖树问题类比，指出类似的问题广泛存在于不同的生态系统中。

• **colek42**：提到tj-actions攻击事件后，开始实施使用“witness-run-action”进行操作签名，以生成签署证明来确保操作的透明性和安全性。

补充讨论：
• **Jenk**：指出GitHub文档中早已提到安全加固的相关内容，并提到某些工具可以警告未使用SHA固定版本的做法。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于GitHub Actions中使用可变标签还是不可变提交ID的选择上。一方认为可变标签是设计使然，并且有助于获取更新，而另一方担心可变标签会导致不可预测的安全风险，倾向于使用固定的提交ID以确保不可变性。

data.title: Scientists break down plastic using a simple, inexpensive catalyst and air
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 北西部大学的研究人员开发了一种简单且经济的方法，利用空气中的湿气分解塑料废物。该过程使用无毒、环保的无溶剂方法，通过廉价的催化剂分解聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）的键，然后暴露在空气中，借助空气中微量的湿气将分解的PET转化为单体，这些单体是塑料的重要 building blocks。该技术比当前的塑料回收方法更安全、清洁、便宜且可持续，为创造塑料的循环经济提供了有希望的途径。该研究已发表在《Green Chemistry》上，解决了塑料废物这一全球紧迫的环境挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料回收的技术、政策、成本及环境影响

不同观点：
• [piokoch] 认为塑料种类繁多，识别材料是回收的主要难题，且当前制度让公民和地方政府承担了回收成本。他建议强制使用单一塑料类型和易移除标签，并指出企业在包装材料选择上的自由导致了环境问题。
• [lxmorj] 提出通过完全燃烧一次性塑料来减少其长期环境影响，认为这样至少能得到两次使用价值，尽管这种方法并不理想。
• [culi] 关注回收技术的效果，尤其是分解成单体的比例和微塑料残留问题，并对当前技术能否解决不可回收塑料提出疑问。

• [Synaesthesia] 强调政府法规的重要性，认为中国禁止一次性塑料是一个有效措施，并指出很多塑料使用是不必要的。

• [voidUpdate] 对新技术能否实际应用持怀疑态度，暗示很多创新技术最终不了了之。

Scientists break down plastic using a simple, inexpensive catalyst and air
by Amanda Morris,
Northwestern University
The photographs show the TPA product formation at different runs after every 4 h of heating (total reaction time = 20 h). Credit:
Green Chemistry
(2025). DOI: 10.1039/D4GC05916F
Harnessing moisture from air, Northwestern University chemists have developed a simple new method for breaking down plastic waste.
The non-toxic, environmentally friendly, solvent-free process first uses an inexpensive catalyst to break apart the bonds in polyethylene terephthalate (PET), the most common plastic in the polyester family. Then, the researchers merely expose the broken pieces to ambient air. Leveraging the trace amounts of moisture in air, the broken-down PET is converted into monomers—the crucial building blocks for plastics. From there, the researchers envision the monomers could be recycled into new PET products or other, more valuable materials.
Safer, cleaner, cheaper and more sustainable than current plastic recycling methods, the new technique offers a promising path toward creating a circular economy for plastics. The study was recently
published
in
Green Chemistry
.
"The U.S. is the number one plastic polluter per capita, and we only recycle 5% of those plastics," said Northwestern's Yosi Kratish, the study's co-corresponding author. "There is a dire need for better technologies that can process different types of
plastic waste
. Most of the technologies that we have today melt down
plastic bottles
and downcycle them into lower-quality products.
"What's particularly exciting about our research is that we harnessed moisture from air to break down the plastics, achieving an exceptionally clean and selective process. By recovering the monomers, which are the basic building blocks of PET, we can recycle or even upcycle them into more valuable materials."
"Our study offers a sustainable and efficient solution to one of the world's most pressing environmental challenges: plastic waste," said Naveen Malik, the study's first author. "Unlike traditional recycling methods, which often produce harmful byproducts like waste salts and require significant energy or chemical inputs, our approach uses a solvent-free process that relies on trace moisture from ambient air. This makes it not only environmentally friendly but also highly practical for real-world applications."
An expert in plastic recycling, Kratish is a research assistant professor of chemistry at Northwestern's Weinberg College of Arts and Sciences. Kratish co-led the study with Tobin J. Marks, the Charles E. and Emma H. Morrison Professor of Chemistry at Weinberg and a professor of materials science and engineering at Northwestern's McCormick School of Engineering. At the time of the research, Malik was an postdoctoral fellow in Marks' laboratory; now he is a research assistant professor at the SRM Institute of Science and Technology in India.
The plastic problem
Commonly used in food packaging and beverage bottles, PET plastics represent 12% of total plastics used globally. Because it does not break down easily, PET is a major contributor to plastic pollution. After use, it either ends up in landfills or, over time, degrades into tiny microplastics or nanoplastics, which often end up in wastewater and waterways.
Finding new ways to recycle plastic is a hot topic in research. But current methods to break down plastics require harsh conditions, including extremely high temperatures, intense energy and solvents, which generate toxic byproducts. The catalysts used in these reactions are also often expensive (like platinum and palladium) or toxic, creating even more harmful waste. Then, after the reaction is performed, researchers have to separate the
recycled materials
from the solvents, which can be a time-consuming and energy-intensive process.
In previous work, Marks' group at Northwestern became the first to develop catalytic processes that do not require solvents. In the new study, the team again devised a solvent-free process.
"Using solvents has many disadvantages," Kratish said. "They can be expensive, and you have to heat them up to high temperatures. Then, after the reaction, you are left with a soup of materials that you have to sort to recover the monomers. Instead of using solvents, we used water vapor from air. It's a much more elegant way to tackle plastic recycling issues."

data.title: In Jail Without a Lawyer: How a Texas Town Fails Poor Defendants
data.author: ceejayoz
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国司法系统的缺陷和不公正问题

不同观点：
• AngryData认为美国司法系统已经破碎，主要问题在于通过法院和警察的费用压榨民众。如果请不起律师，法院提供的公设律师形同虚设。如果请得起律师，问题就变成了是否愿意花费比法院预期压榨的更多钱。如果选择上法庭抗争，还可能面临巨额起诉费用，即使选择认罪也会有额外费用和罚款。总体而言，这个系统只对有钱人有利。

• nadermx引用了一则具体案例，表明在发达国家也存在严重的人权侵犯问题，质疑司法系统的公正性。

• crooked-v认为将司法系统的失败描述为“失败”是一种轻描淡写，实际上这是一种积极的压迫。

• DebtDeflation指出在德克萨斯州，所有交通违法行为（除超速和开放容器外）都是可逮捕的罪行，是否逮捕取决于警察的判断。

• givemeethekeys提到在小而社会保守的社区中，任何突出表现都可能带来严重后果。

• keisborg持有一种“入狱必有因”的观点，认为在押人员必定做过坏事，不能轻易释放坏人。

• FilosofumRex指出大媒体如《纽约时报》倾向于报道红州的司法不公问题，而忽视了蓝州如马萨诸塞州发生的类似问题，并具体描述了在该州发生的警察和检察官腐败案例。

• mmooss质疑为何不使用人身保护令（habeas corpus）来解决这些问题，认为这正是其用途所在。

• tehwebguy以讽刺的语气表示，投票和抗议就能解决这个问题。

• AStonesThrow认为“nolo contendre”（不抗辩）是一种被低估的策略，简单而优雅。

• Avshalom引用了一句格言“系统的目的就是它所做的事”，暗示司法系统的实际运作揭示了其真实目的。

• selimthegrim分享了在路易斯安那州某些农村城镇，地方警察和警长会捏造交通违法行为，将人关押在当地监狱过周末，直到周一法官上班为止，特别是对不喜欢的外来者或活动人士。

• npvrite以讽刺的语气表示，对国家非法监视和警察享有有限豁免权的问题并不惊讶，质疑美国宪法是否被遵守。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于美国司法系统是否仅仅是为有钱人服务，以及是否存在系统性的压迫和腐败。
• 具体案例（如《纽约时报》报道的和FilosofumRex提到的马萨诸塞州案例）引发了对媒体选择性报道的质疑。
• 讨论中还提到了法律工具（如人身保护令）的适用性和有效性问题。
• 不同社区和地区的司法实践差异也被提及，特别是对小城镇和农村地区执法不公的描述。

data.title: Chicago-Sized Iceberg Hid Ancient Ecosystem, Scientists Reveal
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 科学家在亚特兰大洲附近的A-84巨型冰山脱离后，发现了海底存在着丰富的生态系统。利用遥控水下机器人SuBastian，研究团队在1300米深的海底观察到大型珊瑚、海绵以及冰鱼、巨型海蜘蛛和章鱼等多种生物。这些生物群落可能已存在几十年甚至几百年。冰山的脱离让科学家有机会探索原本难以接近的海底区域。研究还显示，洋流对冰层下的生命起着关键作用。虽然冰架的消退令人担忧，但它也为科学探索提供了机会。Schmidt海洋研究所的R/V Falkor（too）研究船将继续在这一领域进行探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：冰鱼及其生态系统的科学发现与环境担忧

不同观点：
• [dmix] 分享了关于冰鱼（Channichthyidae）的科学发现，特别提到它们是已知唯一一种在成年阶段血液中缺乏血红蛋白的脊椎动物。他还引用了2021年2月科学家在南极威德尔海发现的大规模冰鱼繁殖地的例子，该繁殖地约有6000万个活跃巢穴，每个巢穴由一只成年鱼守护，平均每个巢穴有1,735颗卵。

• [Kon-Peki] 用幽默的方式将92平方英里的面积转换为相当于3个不到的德国城市杜塞尔多夫，以此帮助人们理解该区域的大小，没有深入讨论科学内容。

• [DidYaWipe] 以戏谑的语气提到发现了一个“原始深盘披萨，大小如Wrigley Field”，显然是在开玩笑，并没有对科学发现做实质性讨论。

• [jmclnx] 提出了对环境问题的担忧，指出随着冰层迅速融化，这些冰鱼可能正处于生存危机中，暗示气候变化可能威胁到它们的栖息地和生存。

补充讨论：
• 评论中存在科学事实与幽默调侃的混合。虽然[dmix]提供了详细的科学信息和来源，但其他评论如[Kon-Peki]和[DidYaWipe]则以幽默方式回应，没有对主要讨论点做出实质贡献。
• [jmclnx]的评论引入了对气候变化和环境影响的关注，这是对冰鱼生态系统潜在威胁的严肃思考。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于对科学发现的态度，一部分人关注事实和数据，另一部分人则以幽默或讽刺的方式回应，没有深入讨论环境问题的严重性。

The research vessel Falkor (too).
Photo: Schmidt Ocean Institute
Scientists scrutinizing the seafloor beneath a calving iceberg found a remarkable array of living creatures, switching up notions of how the giant chunks of ice affect their immediate environs.
The scientists investigated a region of seafloor recently exposed by the calving of a gigantic icebergâA-84âwhich is as large as Chicago. The team found a surprisingly vibrant community of critters on the seafloor below where A-84 was once attached to an ice shelf attached to Antarctica.
âWe didnât expect to find such a beautiful, thriving ecosystem,” said Patricia Esquete, the expedition’s co-chief scientist and a researcher at the University of Aveiro in Portugal, in a British Antarctic Survey
release
. “Based on the size of the animals, the communities we observed have been there for decades, maybe even hundreds of years.â
Without the 197-square-mile (510-square-kilometer) iceberg in the way, the team was able to scrutinize the seafloor at depths of 4,265 feet (1,300 meters) using the remotely operated vehicle (ROV)
SuBastian
. The team found large corals and sponges supporting other lifeforms, including icefish, giant sea spiders, and octopus.
The scientists who made the discovery were part of a team aboard the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s
R/V Falkor (too)
, a 363-foot-long (111-meter) vessel that’s regularly revealing hidden details of life at the bottom of Earth’s oceans. The vessel has previously
mapped unknown areas
of the ocean floor and even captured the
intimate breeding grounds
of octopuses.
With the icebergs covering the seafloor, organisms below the shelf cannot get nutrients for survival from the surface. The team hypothesized that ocean currents are a critical driver for life beneath the ice sheets. The team also collected data on the larger ice sheet, whose shrinking size spells concern for the animals that live beneath it.
âThe ice loss from the Antarctic Ice Sheet is a major contributor to sea level rise worldwide,â said the expedition’s other co-chief scientist, Sasha Montelli, a researcher at University College London, in the same release. “Our work is critical for providing longer-term context of these recent changes, improving our ability to make projections of future change â projections that can inform actionable policies. We will undoubtedly make new discoveries as we continue to analyze this vital data.â
Though the ice shelf disappearing is worrying, it also creates an opportunity for scientists to explore an area that is otherwise even harder to access.Â
ROV SuBastianÂ
andÂ
R/V Falkor (too)
will almost certainly make new discoveries about extreme environments where life ekes out existence before their journeys are brought to an end.

data.title: Show HN: Feudle – A daily puzzle game built with AI
data.author: papaolivia92
data.article_summary: Feudle是一款在线猜谜游戏，玩家需猜测前一天其他玩家提交的最热门答案。游戏规则简单：猜测热门答案，正确答案会显示在板上并附上回答数量。若三次未猜中即出局。玩家还可以提交自己的问题供未来使用，并查看个人统计数据。游戏提供每日邮件订阅功能，并允许分享结果和投票选择未来调查主题。玩家需登录Google账户以保存游戏进度和查看详细统计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对网站或游戏的体验反馈，包括用户界面、功能建议以及技术实现等方面。

不同观点：
• **关于弹窗订阅**：
  - [nimih] 认为弹窗频率过高，令人反感，甚至影响回访意愿。
  - [skwee357] 也建议移除弹窗，认为其影响用户体验。
  - [roskelld] 理解弹窗的营销目的，但同样觉得弹窗令人反感，建议使用不那么侵入性的方式。
  - [CleverLikeAnOx] 直接称弹窗为“预先的劣化设计”（enshittification），要求移除。

• **关于输入体验**：
  - [nimih] 指出移动端自定义键盘表现不佳，存在卡顿、掉帧、不支持滑动输入等问题，尤其对有可访问性需求的用户不友好。
  - [skwee357] 也提到输入框非原生元素，导致其使用的Vimium插件拦截了输入。

• **关于答案匹配和提示**：
  - [jimmar] 认为答案匹配不够精确，例如输入“meat”时，匹配到“chicken”和“ham”是不合理的，建议对不明确的答案标记为错误。
  - [hatthew] 建议列出错误猜测，以防用户因输入错误或忘记之前猜测而困惑。

• **关于游戏设计与难度**：
  - [oliwary] 认为游戏具有挑战性，但设计合理，适合作为每日挑战游戏，同时提到玩家填写的调查问卷很有创意。
  - [nextts] 认为游戏类似于80年代的电视节目《Family Fortunes》，具有怀旧感。

• **关于技术实现与AI使用**：
  - [madarco] 分享了自己开发的类似游戏，提供了iOS和Android的下载链接。
  - [ks2408] 对游戏中的AI和技术实现表示好奇，询问哪些部分由AI生成，哪些由开发者控制，并询问开发者背景。
  - [davidbek] 对游戏中玩家答案与答案板的匹配机制表示好奇，询问其实现方式。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到弹窗对用户体验的负面影响，表明这是用户普遍关注的问题。
- 输入体验和键盘问题也是移动端用户的一个主要关注点，尤其是对可访问性需求的关注。
- 部分用户对游戏的挑战性和设计给予了积极评价，但也有用户对答案匹配的准确性提出了质疑。
- 技术实现和AI的使用引起了部分用户的兴趣，表明用户对游戏背后的技术细节有一定的好奇心。

文章描述了互联网上正在发生的一场“战争”：AI公司为了训练大型语言模型（LLM），疯狂抓取网络上的高质量数据，目标包括图书馆、档案馆、非营利组织和学术出版商等提供优质信息的网站。这些机构正面临AI公司激进、贪婪且欺骗性的数据抓取行为，尤其是通过无休止的机器人（bots）活动。

过去，传统机器人较为礼貌，遵循网站的规则，但如今的AI机器人无视限制，耗尽服务器资源，给管理和维护这些信息资源的技术人员带来巨大压力。图书馆技术人员正在竭力防御，分享封锁名单和机器人特征，甚至通过屏蔽整个国家的IP或使用第三方服务如Cloudflare来缓解攻击，但效果有限。

这场冲突尤其影响了开放获取（Open Access）网站，例如MIT Press和OAPEN等学术资源平台，因机器人攻击导致服务中断，威胁到公共知识的保存。文章呼吁关注这一问题，以免大量有价值的书籍和信息因AI公司的数据需求而丢失。

主要讨论点：应对网络爬虫和AI生成内容（“AI” bots）引发的问题及解决方案

不同观点：
• [kazinator] 认为过去的爬虫很少造成问题，因为它们遵守robot exclusions和"nofollow"警告。然而，他认为这种说法已经过时，过去二十年里很少有爬虫真正遵守robots.txt。此外，nofollow并不是反爬虫的工具，而是用于告知搜索引擎不对链接内容进行排名提升。

• [pickledoyster] 提出通过法律和网络安全行动（如大量封锁IP、将SDK标记为恶意软件）来打击租用僵尸网络的爬虫活动，并建议从应用商店中清除这些SDK。

• [kragen] 建议使用BitTorrent来解决问题，认为开放获取许可和BitTorrent的对等策略能有效限制自私行为者的危害，并增强对虚假信息和链接失效的抵抗力。他还批评了监控资本主义，主张从监控资本主义手中夺回合法的互联网。

• [xnx] 质疑为何“AI”爬虫引起了如此多的关注，是因为数量庞大，还是因为AI公司各自编写自己的（不良）爬虫程序而不是使用现有的？

• [skeledrew] 认为当前的混乱是迈向语义网的必经之路，主张通过开放数据来民主化AI模型的训练，避免只有少数大公司掌握数据和结果。同时，预测未来大多数查询将通过类似Perplexity的工具进行过滤，因此设置障碍的网站将失去流量。

• [zzo38computer] 提到其HTTP服务器因LLM爬虫的不良行为而受到影响，这些爬虫发出大量无意义的请求，可能导致服务器过载。问题在于这些爬虫的糟糕表现，而非所有爬虫。

• [musicale] 指出爬虫快速消耗连接资源的问题，并质疑CAPTCHA的无效性。

• [elzbardico] 以轻松的语气评论了爬虫的问题。

• [data_maan] 认为使用更复杂的CAPTCHA可以解决问题，并质疑对该问题的过度反应，指出这种爬虫导致的DDOS问题一直存在。

• [josefritzishere] 强烈批评AI，认为其带来的破坏大于实用。

• [nathanaldensr] 主张网络服务器应要求所有客户端使用与真实世界实体（个人或公司实体）绑定的凭证进行身份验证，以便在发生滥用时服务器所有者有法律追索权。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何有效管理和控制爬虫行为，特别是AI生成内容的爬虫。
- 不同解决方案包括技术手段（如CAPTCHA、身份验证）、法律手段（打击僵尸网络）、以及结构性变革（开放数据、语义网）。
- 对AI生成内容的实用性和其引发的问题存在批评和质疑。
- 讨论还涉及对监控资本主义的批评以及对互联网开放性和安全性的关注。

43474196.article_content:
There's a war going on on the Internet. AI companies with billions to burn are hard at work destroying the websites of libraries, archives, non-profit organizations, and scholarly publishers, anyone who is working to make quality information universally available on the internet. And the technologists defending against this broad-based attack are doing everything they can to preserve their outlets while trying to remain true to the mission of providing the digital lifeblood of science and culture to the world.
Yes, many of these beloved institutions are under financial pressures in the current political environment, but politics swings back and forth. The AI armies are only growing more aggressive, more rapacious, more deceitful and ever more numerous.
I'm talking about the voracious hunger of AI companies for good data to train Large Language Models (LLMs). These are the trillion-parameter sets of statistical weights that power things like Claude, ChatGPT and hundreds of systems you've never heard of. Good training data has lots of text, lots of metadata, is reliable and unbiased. It's unsullied by Search Engine Optimization (SEO) practitioners. It doesn't constantly interrupt the narrative flow to try to get you to buy stuff. It's multilingual, subject specific, and written by experts. In other words, it's like a library.
At last week's
Code4lib conference
hosted by Princeton University Library, technologists from across the library world gathered to share information about library systems, how to make them better, how to manage them, and how to keep them running. The hot topic, the thing everyone wanted to talk about, was how to deal with bots from the dark side.
Bots on the internet are nothing new, but a sea change has occurred over the past year. For the past 25 years, anyone running a web server knew that the bulk of traffic was one sort of bot or another. There was googlebot, which was quite polite, and everyone learned to feed it - otherwise no one would ever find the delicious treats we were trying to give away. There were lots of search engine crawlers working to develop this or that service. You'd get "script kiddies" trying thousands of prepackaged exploits. A server secured and patched by a reasonably competent technologist would have no difficulty ignoring these.
The old style bots were rarely a problem. They respected robot exclusions and "nofollow" warnings. The warning helped bots avoid volatile resources and infinite parameter spaces. Even when they ignored exclusions they seemed to be careful about it. They declared their identity in "user-agent" headers. They limited the request rate and number of simultaneous requests to any particular server. Occasionally there would be a malicious bot like a
card-tester
or a
registration spammer
. You'd often have to block these based on IP address. It was part of the landscape, not the dominant feature.
The current generation of bots is mindless. They use as many connections as you have room for. If you add capacity, they just ramp up their requests. They use randomly generated user-agent strings. They come from large blocks of IP addresses. They get trapped in endless hallways. I observed one bot asking for 200,000 nofollow redirect links pointing at Onedrive, Google Drive and Dropbox. (which of course didn't work, but Onedrive decided to stop serving our Canadian human users). They use up server resources - one speaker at Code4lib described a bug where software they were running was using 32 bit integers for session identifiers, and it ran out!
The good guys are trying their best. They're sharing block lists and bot signatures. Many libraries are routinely blocking entire countries (nobody in china could possibly want books!) just to be able to serve a trickle of local requests. They are using commercial services such as Cloudflare to outsource their bot-blocking and captchas, without knowing for sure what these services are blocking, how they're doing it, or whether user privacy and accessibility is being flushed down the toilet. But nothing seems to offer anything but temporary relief. Not that there's anything bad about temporary relief, but we know the bots just intensify their attack on other content stores.
The view of MIT Press's Open-Access site from the Wayback Machine.
The surge of AI bots has hit Open Access sites particularly hard, as their mission conflicts with the need to block bots. Consider that Internet Archive can no longer save snapshots of one of the best open-access publishers, MIT Press
because of cloudflare blocking
. (see above) Who know how many books will be lost this way?  Or consider that the
bots took down OAPEN
, the worlds most important repository of Scholarly OA books, for a day or two. That's 34,000 books that AI "checked out" for two days. Or recent outages at
Project Gutenberg
, which serves 2 million dynamic pages and a half million downloads per day. That's hundreds of thousands of downloads blocked! The link

data.title: Has the decline of knowledge work begun?
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对企业裁员、知识工作及教育的影响

不同观点：
• **Bukhmanizer** 认为，企业进行裁员的原因之一是它们减少了创新和改进工作，将希望寄托于AI，而不是继续进行大量小改进。他们的工作现在几乎只围绕一个概念：AI，且并没有详细的计划如何使用AI实现这些改进。

• **bryanlarsen** 提出相反观点，认为尽管AI提高了知识工作者的生产力，但并不意味着会减少对知识工作者的需求。通过历史对比，如服装制造业的部分自动化导致服装价格下降，需求增加，最终使得更多人从事该行业。因此，AI对知识工作者的需求可能反而会增加。

• **fullshark** 认为，大学学位体系需要彻底反思。当前的学位体系与实际技能需求脱节，导致学生背负沉重的债务，而学位并没有带来相应的工作保障或实际技能。

• **apercu** 对AI的实际效果持怀疑态度，指出当前的AI工具（如ChatGPT）在实际应用中经常出错，使用者需要具备相关知识才能识别和纠正这些错误。因此，虽然AI技术本身很了不起，但过度相信其能力是不可取的。

• **squigglydonut** 认为，如果希望AI产生更好的结果，必须对其提出高要求，仿佛生死攸关。

• **Glyptodon** 认为，知识工作的外包和低薪趋势早在AI普及之前就已经存在，AI只是加剧了这一趋势。AI的引入使得企业可以以更低成本获得尚可的结果，从而减少对高技能员工的需求。

• **7qW24A** 指出，过去10年中企业过度招聘，导致机构臃肿，而AI正好为企业提供了裁员的借口，即使AI并没有显著提升生产力，裁员也可能发生。

• **nopelynopington** 对AI在编写代码方面的能力持怀疑态度，认为即使最好的AI引擎也会写出糟糕的代码，且这种情况可能不会改善。但AI也可能让员工更容易应付工作，从而导致知识工作的整体质量下降。

• **iambateman** 认为，知识工作的技能分布广泛，大多数员工处于中等水平。AI的引入可能提升中等水平员工的能力，使得整体知识工作的平均能力上升。

• **carabiner** 指出，像机械工程等专业领域的知识工作受AI影响较小，因为这些领域的专业数据大多被企业锁住，公开数据较少，难以训练出高效的AI模型。

• **talkingtab** 提出一种更为宏观的社会经济观点，认为AI可能导致企业利润上升但同时减少对人力的需求，最终可能破坏整体经济。此外，企业擅长剥削技术红利，但可能缺乏创新动力。

• **alecco** 认为，像马斯克这样的企业已经通过AI找到了裁员的借口，许多企业可能也随之效仿，将大量工作外包至其他国家，这可能带来潜在的风险。

• **coolThingsFirst** 认为，当前就业市场竞争极其激烈，传统职业发展路径受阻，许多人开始转向小型创业公司或自谋出路。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI是否会真正减少对知识工作者的需求，或者反而会增加需求。
- 大学学位体系的可持续性及其与实际工作需求的脱节问题。
- AI在实际应用中的局限性及其可能带来的负面影响，如错误结果和低质量工作的增加。
- 企业裁员是否主要由AI驱动，或者只是企业借此机会进行结构调整。

data.title: Optimizing ML training with metagradient descent
data.author: ladberg
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种基于元梯度下降（Metagradient Descent, MGD）的方法，用于优化大规模机器学习模型的训练过程。作者提出了一种高效计算元梯度的算法，并引入了一个"平滑模型训练"框架，使得利用元梯度进行有效优化成为可能。实验表明，MGD在数据集选择和抵御数据中毒攻击方面显著优于现有方法，并且能够自动找到具有竞争力的学习率调度策略。该方法为优化模型训练配置提供了新途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于机器学习中超参数优化问题的复杂性以及对相关数学优化理论的讨论。

不同观点：
• [munchler] 认为在实际的机器学习问题中，超参数优化非常复杂且困难。每个训练运行需要很长时间，超参数之间互相影响且对硬件非常敏感，微小的配置调整可能会导致极大的性能差异。这种情况下，没有对问题领域的深入理解很难有效地搜索超参数空间。

• [jn2clark] 提出了“学习如何学习”（learning to learn）的先前工作，并询问该文章为何没有引用相关研究（如论文 https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04474）。这暗示可能存在已有文献中的方法可以用于解决当前讨论的超参数优化问题。

• [MITSardine] 对文章本身进行了深入的数学分析，指出形如 $f : x \to \text{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ 的函数通常不光滑，甚至可能不连续。此外，优化算法通常只能收敛到局部最小值，而非全局最小值。即使在数学上定义良好的情况下，数值计算中的浮点精度问题也会导致实际求解中的困难。MITSardine 还对文章中的符号和定义提出了质疑，认为文章在讨论如何正则化此类函数方面没有给出足够深入的解决方案，并提出了替代符号和定义的建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是超参数优化的实际复杂性以及是否已有其他研究（如“学习如何学习”）可以提供更好的解决方案。[munchler] 强调了实际操作中的难度，而 [jn2clark] 则指向了可能被忽视的相关研究。

• [MITSardine] 详细讨论了优化问题的数学性质，特别是函数 $f$ 的非光滑性和数值计算中的问题，并提出了对文章符号和定义的改进建议。这表明在实际应用中，理论上的优化问题比文章所讨论的更加复杂。

• 讨论中还涉及了具体的数学符号和技术细节问题，如 $\Delta_f$ 符号的使用以及定义中的技术选择，反映了在学术讨论中对精确性和符号一致性的关注。

总体而言，讨论围绕超参数优化的复杂性、已有研究的相关性以及数学优化中的理论问题展开，并包含了对文章具体内容的技术性建议。
