Abstract:
A major challenge in training large-scale machine learning models is configuring the training process to maximize model performance, i.e., finding the best training setup from a vast design space. In this work, we unlock a gradient-based approach to this problem. We first introduce an algorithm for efficiently calculating metagradients -- gradients through model training -- at scale. We then introduce a "smooth model training" framework that enables effective optimization using metagradients. With metagradient descent (MGD), we greatly improve on existing dataset selection methods, outperform accuracy-degrading data poisoning attacks by an order of magnitude, and automatically find competitive learning rate schedules.

data.title: Ruby, Ractors, and lock-free data structures
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Ruby中实现并发数据结构的方法，目标是展示如何在全局可变状态下实现真正的并行处理（当前Ruby内置功能不支持）。文章涉及Ruby、Rust和C等语言，但并非必须精通。示例代码可在GitHub上找到，运行这些代码需要较新版本的Ruby（最好是可本地编译的主分支）、Rust和C编译器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby中的Ractor库的应用与挑战

不同观点：
• **Gibibit的观点**：Gibibit最初对Ractor的认知与Rust的Ractor库混淆了，他认为Rust的Ractor库非常优秀，特别是引入了Erlang/OTP的gen_server actors，值得Rust开发者关注。他对Ruby中的Ractor库文档进行了澄清。
• **Dpflan的观点**：Dpflan提到Mike Perham正在尝试利用Ractor构建可扩展的作业系统，并指出Ractor编程的难点，比如无法访问词法作用域或闭包变量，这使得Ractor编程变得复杂，甚至像是一种新的Ruby方言。他还将Ractor与Goroutines进行了类比，指出学习曲线可能类似。
• **T-writescode的观点**：T-writescode对Ractor是否真正遵循了actor模型提出疑问，尤其是邮件箱机制是否已经解决。他担心人们在使用Ractor时可能强迫actor模型遵循不合适的并行编程范式。同时，他对文章中过多提及Rust表示不解。
• **Kodablah的观点**：Kodablah提到他们的Ruby项目因使用Google Protobuf库而无法使用Ractor，因为该库不是Ractor安全的，并且无法要求用户不使用官方的Protobuf库。

补充讨论：
• **Rco8786的观点**：Rco8786认为，一个生产就绪的Ractor安全数据结构库将大大推动Ractor的采用，解决目前许多人遇到的主要障碍。

争议焦点：
• Ractor是否真正实现了actor模型，特别是邮件箱机制是否完善。
• Ractor编程的复杂性，特别是对词法作用域和闭包变量访问的限制，使得Ractor编程变得困难。
• 在Ruby项目中使用Ractor时，现有库（如Google Protobuf）的兼容性问题。

Intro
This story is about concurrent data structures in the context of Ruby. The goal here is to demonstrate how true parallelism can be achieved with global mutable state (which at the time of writing, is not supported by built-in Ruby primitives).
Familiarity with Ruby, Rust, C, (and a bit of other tooling) is nice to have, but hopefully not mandatory.
The repository with code examples can be found
on GitHub
, to run it you need a relatively new version of Ruby (master branch is probably the best option if you can compile it locally), Rust and C compilers.

data.title: Svelte: $derived can now be overwritten
data.author: jedeusus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了Svelte项目中一个重要的代码合并（PR）：使派生值（derived values）变为可写。该合并由Rich-Harris在2025年3月21日完成，涉及将8个提交合并到主分支。文章详细说明了如何在提交PR前确保其合理性，包括引用相关问题、创建RFC以及进行测试和文档更新。此外，还提供了有关更改的文档预览和Playground链接。代码变更将在下一个版本中发布，类型为次要更新。讨论中有人担心使派生值可写可能会违背用户期望并影响优化，但也有开发者指出变量仍可设为只读，且派生值本质上具有可变性。最终，该PR被成功合并并关闭了相关问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Svelte 5及其新特性（特别是runes）在实际开发中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• **benton**：认为Svelte 5中的runes虽然是对之前版本的改进，但在处理复杂状态时仍然过于“魔法化”，增加了心智负担。他提到随着项目增长，调试问题和反应性丢失的情况越来越多，觉得这并不实用。他还将Svelte的魔法语法与Vue的更直观的反应性模型做了对比。
  
• **joseneca**：理解runes的实现原因，但个人不喜欢。他觉得runes削弱了Svelte原有的简洁语法，认为这种变化是在向不好的方向妥协。

• **orefalo**：非常喜欢Svelte 5和runes，认为它们提供了一个无缝的开发体验，能够快速掌握类似于JS/HTML的概念，相比其他选项学习成本更低，并希望这些更新能更早推出。

• **randysalami**：目前正在使用C#和EventStoreDB等技术构建后端，前端两年前用Svelte做了一个PoC应用，非常享受编写和设计的过程，期待使用Svelte的新更新进行二次开发。

• **yewenjie**：询问那些已经将大型生产代码库迁移到Svelte 5的开发者的开发体验如何。

• **arcanemachiner**：作为一个没有使用过Svelte 5的人，询问这次更改的意义是什么。

• **benatkin**：对Svelte 5中的一个简单乐观UI例子表示惊讶，并提到想知道Solid的作者Ryan Carniato对这一更新的看法。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Svelte 5中runes的引入是否增加了开发者的心智负担。benton认为runes让调试和反应性问题变得更加复杂，而orefalo则非常喜欢runes和Svelte 5带来的开发体验。

• **不同背景的开发者**：randysalami从其他技术栈的角度表达了对Svelte更新的期待，而arcanemachiner则希望了解Svelte 5更新的基本意义。

• **与其他框架的比较**：benton将Svelte与Vue的反应性模型进行了对比，提出了Svelte在处理复杂状态时的不足。

• **对新特性的具体例子**：benatkin提到了Svelte 5中一个具体的简单例子，并对该例子的效果表示惊讶，同时提到想了解其他框架作者对这一更新的看法。

data.title: Sell yourself, sell your work
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 文章强调，仅仅完成出色的工作并不足够，还需要主动宣传和分享，才能让世界受益并实现个人价值的最大化。作者指出，许多人虽然技术出色，但不愿意花时间撰写报告或分享成果，导致他们的工作无法被外界了解。因此，为了让他人知道并利用你的工作成果，必须克服对“宣传”的抵触心理，积极传播自己的成就。简而言之，做好工作后，还需要有效地“推销”自己和自己的工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该公开和宣传自己的项目和作品，以及这样做是否是实现作品和个人价值的前提。

不同观点：
• **支持公开和宣传**：Simonw 认为，记录和分享项目非常重要，尤其是通过博客或GitHub，这样不仅能防止项目过时，还能让更多人受益。他还提到自己后悔没有记录早期项目。Gyello 也分享了自己通过为亲友创建项目并展示这些项目所获得的满足感，尽管这些项目没有公开发布。

• **反对强制公开**：Henchman21 和 Iaaan 持反对意见，认为不是所有作品都必须公开或商业化才能体现其价值。Iaaan 强调，人们有权选择是否分享自己的创作，而不应被外界压力左右。Henchman21 进一步指出，作品的价值不一定在于商业化，人类努力的价值超越金钱。

• **强调内在价值**：Sashank_1509 引用了Albert Jay Nock的《Isiah’s Job》一文，认为真正卓越的工作不需要通过宣传来体现其价值，时间会证明其意义。Bravetraveler 和 Ryandrake 也认为，可靠性和个人的内在满足感比宣传更为重要，做好工作自然会有人关注。

• **中立或实用主义**：Boznz 和 Stocknoob 持中立态度，认为宣传与否取决于个人喜好和需求。Boznz 提到自己不擅长营销，但意识到记录和分享项目可能带来机会。Stocknoob 建议年轻程序员专注于自己的兴趣，而不是自我宣传，除非他们喜欢这样做。

补充讨论：
• **个人品牌和商业化**：Webprofusion 和 Rednafi 提到公开项目和写作有助于建立个人品牌，可能会带来职业机会。然而，Rednafi 也警告不要过度销售，否则可能适得其反。

• **批判商业化压力**：Bjornsing 指出，人们往往忽视了从他人工作中筛选出有价值的部分，而不是被营销牵着走。Maxlin 则用比喻说明，人类生活的意义在于自我满足，而非对外展示。

争议焦点：作品的价值是否需要通过公开和商业化来体现，以及是否应由外界压力决定个人是否应该分享自己的创作。

data.title: Devs say AI crawlers dominate traffic, forcing blocks on entire countries
data.author: LinuxBender
data.article_summary:
软件开发者Xe Iaso遭遇亚马逊的AI爬虫流量攻击，导致其Git服务频繁不稳定和停机。尽管采取了多种防御措施，爬虫仍通过伪造用户代理和使用住宅IP代理绕过限制。Iaso最终创建了名为"Anubis"的系统，要求浏览器在访问前解决计算谜题，以此阻挡爬虫。然而，这种方法也给合法用户带来了延迟问题。

这一问题在开源社区广泛存在，许多项目的基础设施因AI爬虫而过载，导致服务不稳定和带宽成本上升。例如，Fedora Pagure项目不得不屏蔽巴西的所有流量，GNOME GitLab则采用了类似Anubis的系统，结果显示大部分请求是自动化的。

开源项目通常资源有限，面对AI爬虫的侵扰，维护者们感到负担沉重。例如，Inkscape项目的Martin Owens提到，他们的问题不仅来自传统的DDoS攻击，还包括一些公司无视规则、伪造浏览器信息。

社区对AI公司占用大量资源的行为感到不满，认为这些公司不尊重公共资源，且对受影响项目的诉求反应迟钝。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络上的数据抓取和机器人流量的管理及其影响

不同观点：
• **公司应采取更协作的方式进行数据抓取**：tedunangst认为，公司应该采取更协作的方式，比如限速数据抓取，以免压垮目标网站。如果目标网站在抓取后下线，那反而是“功能”。
• **机器人流量的快速攻击现象**：Nckpz分享了自己新项目在24小时内遭到大量垃圾表单提交攻击的经历，尽管没有对外宣传，但机器人迅速攻击了服务器。
• **激进的AI机器人对内容网站的影响**：ipaddr提到，由于激进的AI机器人，他们不得不关闭多个内容网站，这些机器人无视robots文件，导致服务器宕机。
• **特定AI机器人造成的DoS攻击**：rco8786描述了由Anthropic的ClaudeBot引发的DoS攻击，导致网站带宽超限，必须手动处理。

补充讨论：
• **反机器人措施的有效性与浏览器垄断问题**：userbinator指出，复杂的JS反机器人措施可能加剧浏览器垄断，建议使用简单HTML表单提问，以防止LLM（大型语言模型）破解。
• **对机器人检测和应对策略的建议**：edoloughlin提出了一种调皮的策略，即检测到AI机器人时，向其提供随机数据，让它们也感受到痛苦。
• **开源许可证的更新需求**：ANarrativeApe质疑是否需要根据当前机器人滥用行为更新开源许可证，以使这种滥用行为公开化。
• **创建私有网络的讨论**：haswell考虑创建一个类似“亲友”的私有网络，以重获发布信息的自由。
• **国家封锁和爬虫监管**：ggm认为，国家封锁是懒惰且不实用的，爬虫应该支付“愚蠢税”或被监管。
• **对不同类型网站的影响**：grotorea质疑这种现象是否仅影响非营利网站，并担心更严格的登录墙会导致网络内容向深层网络迁移。

争议焦点：
• **如何有效管理机器人流量和数据抓取行为**，包括技术手段（如反机器人措施）和政策手段（如爬虫监管、许可证更新）。
• **机器人流量的快速攻击和DoS攻击的普遍性及其对不同类型网站的影响**。

Software developer Xe Iaso
reached a breaking point
earlier this year when aggressive AI crawler traffic from Amazon overwhelmed their Git repository service, repeatedly causing instability and downtime. Despite configuring standard defensive measures—adjusting robots.txt, blocking known crawler user-agents, and filtering suspicious traffic—Iaso found that AI crawlers continued evading all attempts to stop them, spoofing user-agents and cycling through residential IP addresses as proxies.
Desperate for a solution, Iaso eventually resorted to moving their server behind a VPN and creating "Anubis," a custom-built proof-of-work challenge system that forces web browsers to solve computational puzzles before accessing the site. "It's futile to block AI crawler bots because they lie, change their user agent, use residential IP addresses as proxies, and more," Iaso wrote in a
blog post
titled "a desperate cry for help." "I don't want to have to close off my Gitea server to the public, but I will if I have to."
Iaso's story highlights a broader crisis rapidly spreading across the open source community, as what appear to be aggressive AI crawlers increasingly overload community-maintained infrastructure, causing what amounts to persistent distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on vital public resources. According to a
comprehensive recent report
from LibreNews, some open source projects now see as much as 97 percent of their traffic originating from AI companies' bots, dramatically increasing bandwidth costs, service instability, and burdening already stretched-thin maintainers.
Kevin Fenzi, a member of the Fedora Pagure project's sysadmin team,
reported on his blog
that the project had to block all traffic from Brazil after repeated attempts to mitigate bot traffic failed. GNOME GitLab implemented Iaso's "Anubis" system, requiring browsers to solve computational puzzles before accessing content. GNOME sysadmin Bart Piotrowski
shared
on Mastodon that only about 3.2 percent of requests (2,690 out of 84,056) passed their challenge system, suggesting the vast majority of traffic was automated. KDE's GitLab infrastructure was temporarily knocked offline by crawler traffic originating from Alibaba IP ranges, according to LibreNews, citing a KDE Development chat.
While Anubis has proven effective at filtering out bot traffic, it comes with drawbacks for legitimate users. When many people access the same link simultaneously—such as when a GitLab link is shared in a chat room—site visitors can face significant delays. Some mobile users have reported waiting up to two minutes for the proof-of-work challenge to complete, according to the news outlet.
The situation isn't exactly new. In December, Dennis Schubert, who maintains infrastructure for the Diaspora social network,
described
the situation as "literally a DDoS on the entire internet" after discovering that AI companies accounted for 70 percent of all web requests to their services.
The costs are both technical and financial. The Read the Docs project reported that blocking AI crawlers immediately decreased their traffic by 75 percent, going from 800GB per day to 200GB per day. This change saved the project approximately $1,500 per month in bandwidth costs, according to their blog post "AI crawlers need to be more respectful."
A disproportionate burden on open source
The situation has created a tough challenge for open source projects, which rely on public collaboration and typically operate with limited resources compared to commercial entities. Many maintainers have reported that AI crawlers deliberately circumvent standard blocking measures, ignoring robots.txt directives, spoofing user agents, and rotating IP addresses to avoid detection.
As LibreNews reported, Martin Owens from the Inkscape project
noted
on Mastodon that their problems weren't just from "the usual Chinese DDoS from last year, but from a pile of companies that started ignoring our spider conf and started spoofing their browser info." Owens added, "I now have a prodigious block list. If you happen to work for a big company doing AI, you may not get our website anymore."
On Hacker News, commenters in threads
about the LibreNews
post last week and a
post on Iaso's battles
in January expressed deep frustration with what they view as AI companies' predatory behavior toward open source infrastructure. While these comments come from forum posts rather than official statements, they represent a common sentiment among developers.
As one Hacker News user
put it
, AI firms are operating from a position that "goodwill is irrelevant" with their "$100bn pile of capital." The discussions depict a battle between smaller AI startups that have worked collaboratively with affected projects and larger corporations that have been unresponsive despite allegedly forcing thousan

软件开发者Xe Iaso遭遇亚马逊的AI爬虫流量攻击，导致其Git服务频繁不稳定和停机。尽管采取了多种防御措施，爬虫仍通过伪造用户代理和使用住宅IP代理绕过限制。Iaso最终创建了名为"Anubis"的系统，要求浏览器在访问前解决计算谜题，以此阻挡爬虫。然而，这种方法也给合法用户带来了延迟问题。

这一问题在开源社区广泛存在，许多项目的基础设施因AI爬虫而过载，导致服务不稳定和带宽成本上升。例如，Fedora Pagure项目不得不屏蔽巴西的所有流量，GNOME GitLab则采用了类似Anubis的系统，结果显示大部分请求是自动化的。

开源项目通常资源有限，面对AI爬虫的侵扰，维护者们感到负担沉重。例如，Inkscape项目的Martin Owens提到，他们的问题不仅来自传统的DDoS攻击，还包括一些公司无视规则、伪造浏览器信息。

社区对AI公司占用大量资源的行为感到不满，认为这些公司不尊重公共资源，且对受影响项目的诉求反应迟钝。

data.title: Better Shell History Search
data.author: ltratt
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何通过改进Unix终端中的命令历史搜索功能来提高工作效率。作者指出，许多人由于不熟悉快捷操作而浪费时间在重复输入命令上。虽然Bash等壳允许使用Ctrl-r进行子字符串搜索，但这种方法较为局限。作者推荐结合使用Ctrl-r和工具fzf，实现模糊搜索并同时显示多个匹配结果，大大提升了查找命令的速度和准确性。作者亲身体验表明，这一组合显著提高了其工作效率，并促使他更大胆地使用复杂命令。最后，作者还提到发现了另一个工具skim，相比fzf更符合其需求。尽管如此，作者认为无论选择哪个工具，都能显著提升Unix用户的效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： shell历史搜索工具的比较与改进建议

不同观点：
• **支持Atuin的多设备同步功能**：[jakebasile]认为Atuin非常有价值，尤其是在多台设备上使用时，可以保持历史记录同步，还可以按主机或目录进行筛选。
• **推荐zsh插件**：[northisup]建议使用zsh的zle插件，如history-search-multi-word和fast-syntax-highlighting，认为这些插件提供了良好的性能和语法高亮功能。
• **McFly的智能搜索**：[devjam]推荐McFly，它可以根据工作目录和最近执行的命令进行智能搜索和实时优先级排序。
• **fzf与bash自动补全的整合需求**：[worldsayshi]希望fzf能与bash自动补全整合，以获得更像代码补全的体验，并提到fzf-tab可能是一个解决方案，但仅适用于zsh。
• **对功能过载的担忧**：[fsckboy]担心新功能会打破原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖，并提到Linux中的一些功能逐渐消失，如中键粘贴。
• **Atuin与fzf/skim的比较**：[3r7j6qzi9jvnve]认为Atuin的模糊匹配不如fzf/skim，更倾向于使用skim的shell整合功能。
• **推荐hstr**：[bramgn]推荐hstr，认为这是一个很好的历史搜索工具，尽管自己没有广泛使用其他工具。
• **zsh-histdb的优点**：[Hobadee]使用zsh-histdb，并赞赏它显示返回状态和执行命令的目录功能。
• **Atuin的网络安全问题**：[joshka]解释Atuin的网络功能可以完全编译出来，并且历史记录是端到端加密的，认为其安全性足够好。

补充讨论：
• **共享历史记录的价值**：[larusso]认为共享历史记录在不同窗口/标签之间很重要，但对一些人来说可能存在争议，尤其是当重复执行某些命令时。
• **改进历史记录的功能建议**：[wodenokoto]希望历史记录能显示命令执行的位置、是否失败以及添加常用命令/收藏。
• **Bacon替代重复命令执行**：[joshka]提到Bacon可以替代重复执行的命令，如cargo test。
• **对新手的批评**：[SrslyJosh]批评不熟悉基础shell命令的人，并建议学习bash/zsh/sh以及基本工具如grep、sed、awk等。

争议焦点：
• **新功能与用户习惯的冲突**：一些用户（如[fsckboy]）担心新功能会破坏原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖。
• **工具的选择与偏好**：不同用户对工具的偏好不同，如Atuin、fzf、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，各有优缺点。

总结：
评论主要围绕shell历史搜索工具的功能、改进建议以及用户习惯的冲突展开。不同用户根据自己的需求和偏好推荐了不同的工具，如Atuin、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，并提出了一些功能改进建议，如整合fzf与bash自动补全、显示命令执行位置和是否失败等。同时，也有用户对新功能与原有用户习惯的冲突表示担忧。

I spend an awful lot of my day in Unix terminals running shell commands. For
some reason, the variance in efficiency between different people when using the shell
is huge: I know people who can run rings around me, and Iâve come across
more than one paid professional who doesnât use the âupâ key to retrieve the
previous command.
I chose that last example very deliberately: most of the commands most of us
run in the shell are highly repetitive. I typically run around 50-100 unique
(i.e. syntactically distinct) shell commands per working day
[1]
â but
Iâll often run a tiny subset of those commands (e.g.
cargo test
) hundreds of
time in a single day.
Since many command-line tools have hard-to-remember options, we can save huge
chunks of time â not to mention make fewer errors â if we can search our
shell history to find a previous incantation of a command we want to run. In
this post Iâm going to show how, with little effort, searching shell
history can look like this:
[Video]
Searching shell history
Larger Unix shells such as Bash have long allowed users to search through their
shell history by pressing
Ctrl-r
and entering a substring. If I (in order)
executed the commands
cat /etc/motd
then
cat /etc/rc.conf
, then
Ctrl-r
followed by âcatâ will first match
cat /etc/rc.conf
; pressing
Ctrl-r
again
will cycle backwards for the next match which is
cat /etc/motd
. I almost
never used this feature, because substring matching is too crude.
For example, I may know the command I want is
cat
, the leaf
name Iâm looking for is
motd
but I donât remember the directory: substring
matching canât help me find what Iâm looking for. Instead, I regularly used
grep
(with wildcards) to search through my shellâs history file instead.
For me, the game changer was pairing
Ctrl-r
with
fzf
, which brought two changes. First,
matching is âfuzzyâ, so I can type âc moâ and
cat /etc/motd
will be
matched. Second, multiple matches are shown at once. Typing âcatâ will show
me several
cat
commands, allowing me to quickly select the right
incantation (which may not have been the most recent).
Itâs difficult for me to overstate how powerful a feature this is. Few things
in life make me as happy as pressing
ctrl-R
then typing â
l1
â and having a 100
character command-line execution that runs a complicated debugging tool, with
multiple environment variables set, whose output gets put in
/tmp/l1
appear
in my terminal.
Using
Ctrl-r
and fzf roughly doubled my efficiency in the shell
overnight. Interestingly, it had an even greater long term effect: I became a
more ambitious user of shell commands because I knew I could outsource my
memory to fzf. For example, since itâs now very easy to recall past commands, I
no longer set global environment variables, which had previously caused me
grief when I forgot about them
[2]
. Now I set environment variables on a
per-command basis, knowing that I can recall them with
Ctrl-r
and fzf.
For many years my favoured shell was zsh. When I later moved from zsh to fish,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was the first thing I configured; and when I moved back to zsh
[3]
, and redid my configuration from scratch,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was again the first
thing I got working (shortly followed by
autosuggestions
). If you
take nothing else from this
post than â
Ctrl-r
and fzf are a significant productivity boon for Unix
usersâ, then I will have done something useful.
No tool, of course, is perfect. A
couple of months back I somehow stumbled across
skim
, an fzf-alike that out-of-the-box
happens to suit me just a little bit better than fzf. The differences
are mostly minor, and you wonât go far wrong with either tool. That said,
I find that skimâs matching more often finds the commands I want quickly,
I prefer skimâs UI, and I find it easier to install skim on
random boxes â small advantages, perhaps, but enough for switching to be
worth it for me.
Doing even better
Finding Skim encouraged me to quickly look around to see what else in this sphere might
improve my productivity. I quickly came across
Atuin
, which is a much
more sophisticated shell history recording mechanism: the video on its front
page showed a much nicer matching UI than I had previously considered possible.
However, I quickly realised Atuin wasnât for me or, at least, wasnât easily for
me.

data.title: Show HN: A website for sharing the "Good, Bad, and Why"s of urban spaces
data.author: kappasan
data.article_summary: 《Community Atlas of Urban Phenomena》是一个让用户分享和标记城市中各种现象的平台，用户可以根据体验将现象标记为"Good"（好）、"Bad"（坏）、"Why"（为什么）等标签，并添加评论和照片。内容涵盖设计、艺术、文化、交通、基础设施、技术、安全、健康、自然、环境、商业等多个方面。用户发布的帖子示例包括对特别建筑、城市设施、交通问题等的评价，如"1000日元卡住了"、"イベント会場へのナビゲーション"（活动会场的导航）、"マンホール周りの印"（井盖周围的标记）等。平台还提供按地区、时间、标签等筛选功能，但存在一些功能不完善的问题，如评论功能不稳定，开发者承诺在下一版本中改进。

43465740.article_summary: 《Community Atlas of Urban Phenomena》是一个让用户分享和标记城市中各种现象的平台，用户可以根据体验将现象标记为"Good"（好）、"Bad"（坏）、"Why"（为什么）等标签，并添加评论和照片。内容涵盖设计、艺术、文化、交通、基础设施、技术、安全、健康、自然、环境、商业等多个方面。用户发布的帖子示例包括对特别建筑、城市设施、交通问题等的评价，如"1000日元卡住了"、"イベント会場へのナビゲーション"（活动会场的导航）、"マンホール周りの印"（井盖周围的标记）等。平台还提供按地区、时间、标签等筛选功能，但存在一些功能不完善的问题，如评论功能不稳定，开发者承诺在下一版本中改进。
43465740.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个网站的功能、内容和可访问性的多方面讨论

不同观点：
• sinuhe69认为，增加自动翻译功能将使网站对更广泛的受众开放，提高可访问性。
• sgc指出，在Linux上的Firefox浏览器使用时，图片无法在详情页加载，需要借助谷歌翻译来阅读网站内容，并提供了相关页面的链接。
• cc101对网站上展示的某张海报表示不满，认为其包含种族和文化偏见的内容，并对此种内容被容忍感到不安。

补充讨论：
• ripley12对网站表示赞赏，并计划在有空时添加关于温哥华的相关条目。
• bythreads表示喜欢网站的简洁设计，并提到AI机器人可能会喜欢抓取该网站。
• chachan表达了对网站的怀旧情感，认为这是他怀念的互联网风格。
• upghost分享了自己在探索该网站时，发现了iOS的翻译功能变得更好了，并对网站开发者表示感谢。
• kappasan作为原贴作者（OP），说明了注册表单要求填写电子邮件地址只是作为用户ID使用，非有效地址也可以，但提醒如果忘记密码将无法重置。
• mc3301表示自己有空时会添加许多关于日本的相关条目。
• riffic认为网站很像"模式语言"(Pattern Language)，并希望这种网站在他所在的地区流行起来，同时提供了维基百科上关于"模式语言"的链接。

争议焦点：
• cc101提出的种族和文化偏见问题，与其他用户对网站内容的积极评价形成对比，表明在内容审核和包容性方面存在潜在争议。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ghidra与LLM（大型语言模型）集成的效果和实用性

不同观点：
• mdaniel认为之前Ghidra与LLM集成的案例展示出了良好的效果，并分享了一个视频链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42860849）作为参考，显示出对这种集成持积极态度。

• Malimite提到了一篇关于iOS和macOS反编译工具的文章（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42829402），这可能暗示了在特定平台上应用此类工具的潜力，虽然未明确表态，但提供了另一个视角来审视Ghidra与LLM的结合。

• brokensegue则基于自己的经验，对直接将Ghidra内容复制到LLM并期望其自动解析的效果表示怀疑。他指出这种方法并不总是成功，并建议为这类集成工作制定一些基准以衡量效果，显示出对实际效果的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Ghidra与LLM集成在实际应用中的有效性。mdaniel看到了积极的案例，而brokensegue则基于个人经验提出了质疑，认为缺乏明确的成功标准和基准。

• 不同评论者提供了外部资源链接，为讨论提供了更多背景信息和具体案例，帮助更全面地理解Ghidra与LLM集成的应用场景和潜在问题。

• brokensegue的建议指出了一个实际问题，即在技术应用中，需要有明确的衡量标准和基准来评估新工具和方法的有效性。

data.title: Chewing gum can shed microplastics into saliva, pilot study finds
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 一项初步研究发现，嚼口香糖可能会将数百至数千个微塑料颗粒释放到唾液中并被摄入。美国化学学会（ACS）2025年春季会议上发表的这项研究显示，无论是天然还是合成口香糖，都会在咀嚼过程中释放微塑料。研究测试了五种合成口香糖和五种天然口香糖，结果发现每克口香糖平均释放约100个微塑料，有些甚至高达600个。一个大的口香糖可能释放多达3000个塑料颗粒。如果按每人每年嚼160至180根口香糖计算，可能摄入约30,000个微塑料。研究还发现，微塑料主要在前两分钟内脱落，且天然和合成口香糖的释放量相似，均含有聚烯烃等塑料成分。研究人员强调，虽然尚未确定微塑料对人体的危害，但建议人们采取措施减少暴露。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：口香糖中塑料成分的来源、分类及其影响

不同观点：
• **[ricardobeat]** 对口香糖中“天然”成分的定义表示怀疑，质疑其中塑料的来源，是否是误标或欺诈行为。他希望了解这些塑料是如何被定义和归类的。

• **[xattt]** 关心塑料在口香糖中如何释放出来，并提出疑问：这些塑料碎片在再次咀嚼时是否会重新整合回口香糖中，进而影响其对环境或人体的影响。

• **[more-nitor]** 认为将所有塑料成分简单地标记为“微塑料”是不准确的。他指出不同的塑料种类（如聚乙烯、聚丙烯等）可能会有不同的化学性质和影响，应该区别对待，而不是一概而论。

• **[wkat4242]** 对现代口香糖含有塑料成分并不感到意外，指出由于天然成分成本过高，使用塑料替代是当今普遍的做法。他隐含了对市场因成本考虑而放弃天然成分的批评。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于口香糖中塑料成分的来源、分类和影响是否得到了充分解释和正确标记。
• 不同讨论者对于塑料在口香糖中的存在形式、对环境和健康的影响有不同的关注点，有人质疑标记的准确性，有人关心塑料的物理行为，还有人关注不同塑料种类的具体影响。
• 市场经济因素也被提及，天然成分因成本问题被塑料替代，反映了消费品行业中成本和质量之间的权衡。

Chewing gum can shed microplastics into saliva, pilot study finds
PressPacs
March 25, 2025

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Lea este comunicado de prensa en español
SAN DIEGO, March 25, 2025 — Plastic is everywhere. And many products we use in everyday life, such as
cutting boards
,
clothes
and
cleaning sponges
, can expose people to tiny, micrometer-wide plastic particles called microplastics. Now, chewing gum could be added to the list. In a pilot study, researchers found that chewing gum can release hundreds to thousands of microplastics per piece into saliva and potentially be ingested.
The researchers will present their results at the spring meeting of the American Chemical Society (ACS). ACS Spring 2025 is being held March 23-27; it features about 12,000 presentations on a range of science topics.
Both natural and synthetic chewing gums released microplastics into saliva in a pilot study.
New Africa/Shutterstock.com
“Our goal is not to alarm anybody,” says Sanjay Mohanty, the project’s principal investigator and an engineering professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA). “Scientists don’t know if microplastics are unsafe to us or not. There are no human trials. But we know we are exposed to plastics in everyday life, and that’s what we wanted to examine here.”
Animal studies and studies with human cells show that microplastics could cause harm, so while we wait for more definitive answers from the scientific community, individuals can take steps to reduce their exposure to microplastics.
Scientists estimate that humans consume tens of thousands of microplastics
(between 1 micrometer- and 5 millimeters-wide) every year through foods, drinks, plastic packaging, coatings, and production or manufacturing processes. Yet, chewing gum as a potential source of microplastics hasn’t been widely studied, despite the candy’s worldwide popularity. So, Mohanty and a graduate student in his lab, Lisa Lowe, wanted to identify how many microplastics a person could potentially ingest from chewing natural and synthetic gums.
Chewing gums are made from a rubbery base, sweetener, flavorings and other ingredients. Natural gum products use a plant-based polymer, such as chicle or other tree sap, to achieve the right chewiness, while other products use synthetic rubber bases from petroleum-based polymers.
“Our initial hypothesis was that the synthetic gums would have a lot more microplastics because the base is a type of plastic,” says Lowe, who started the project as an undergraduate intern at UCLA and the presenter of this research.
The researchers tested five brands of synthetic gum and five brands of natural gum, all of which are commercially available. Mohanty says they wanted to reduce the human factor of varied chewing patterns and saliva, so they had seven pieces from each brand all chewed by one person.
In the lab, the person chewed the piece of gum for 4 minutes, producing samples of saliva every 30 seconds, then a final mouth rinse with clean water, all of which got combined into a single sample. In another experiment, saliva samples were collected periodically over 20 minutes to look at the release rate of microplastics from each piece of gum. Then, the researchers measured the number of microplastics present in each saliva sample. Plastic particles were either stained red and counted under a microscope or analyzed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, which also provided the polymer composition.
Lowe measured an average of 100 microplastics released per gram of gum, though some individual gum pieces released as many as 600 microplastics per gram. A typical piece of gum weighs between 2 and 6 grams, meaning a large piece of gum could release up to 3,000 plastic particles. If the average person chews 160 to 180 small sticks of gum per year, the researchers estimated that could result in the ingestion of around 30,000 microplastics. If the average person consumes tens of thousands of microplastics per year, gum chewing could greatly increase the ingested amount.
“Surprisingly, both synthetic and natural gums had similar amounts of microplastics released when we chewed them,” says Lowe. And they also contained the same polymers: polyolefins, polyethylene terephthalates, polyacrylamides and polystyrenes. The most abundant polymers for both types of gum were polyolefins, a group of plastics that includes polyethylene and polypropylene.
Most of the microplastics detached from gum within the first 2 minutes of chewing. But Mohanty says they weren’t released because of enzymes in saliva breaking them down. Rather, the act of chewing is abrasive enough to make pieces flake off. And after 8 minutes of chewing, 94% of the plastic particles collected during the tests had been released. data.title: Toyota's 'Circular Factory' Idea Could Be a Great Alternative to Junk Yards
data.author: zfg
data.article_summary: 丰田汽车通过其新启动的丰田循环工厂（TCF）项目，致力于减少报废车辆（ELVs）对环境的影响，并挖掘其经济价值。该项目将在欧盟市场首先实施，首家工厂位于英国的丰田汽车制造工厂。通过该项目，报废车辆将经过验证、拆解，其材料和零件将被分类用于再利用、再制造和回收。丰田计划每年回收10,000辆报废车辆，并将其中的120,000个零件重新销售，同时回收300吨高纯度塑料和8,200吨钢材等材料。该项目不仅旨在减少环境污染，还计划在全欧洲推广，并与其他组织合作推动循环经济和碳中和目标。相比美国的“旧车换现金”计划，丰田的举措更具可持续性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对OEM厂商控制二手汽车零部件市场的担忧及其实际可行性

不同观点：
• [potato3732842的观点] 认为OEM厂商推动集中化处理二手汽车零部件的举措，是为了加强对市场的控制，目的是限制独立 junkyard 的存在。他们可能通过声称某些零件"不可修复"来拒绝销售，从而削弱二手市场。论据包括对OEM厂商垄断动机的怀疑和对市场自由流通的担忧。

• [calmbonsai的观点] 不同意potato3732842的看法，认为OEM厂商不可能实现这种控制。该评论指出，德国激励措施更高，且大众的类似计划已经失败。此外，现有的重型农用设备市场例子显示，OEM厂商垄断不会成功。该评论还指出，二手零件市场利润丰厚，OEM厂商垄断只会导致产品内置的报废策略和创新不足。

• [1970-01-01的观点] 提出一个实际问题，即汽车设计更新换代导致旧零件最终无法继续流通。他们认为，随着时间推移，旧零件的储存和分类将占用过多空间，超出junkyard的处理能力。这暗示了依赖二手零件市场的实际操作困难。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于OEM厂商是否能够成功控制或垄断二手零件市场，以及这种控制对市场自由和创新的潜在负面影响。
- 论据中提到了德国激励政策、大众的失败案例以及重型农用设备市场的现有情况，作为OEM厂商难以垄断二手市场的证据。
- 另一个值得注意的点是关于旧零件储存和处理的实际问题，这与市场运作的可行性相关联。

43476244.article_content:
Getty Images
With one junked car at a time, Toyota looks to reduce, reuse, and recycle its way into another profit stream while keeping trash out of well, actual streams. We’ve seen plenty of press releases describing sustainability and other green initiatives, but we have not seen many automakers talking about taking responsibility for its cars decades after they’re built. This could be an interesting idea.
The Toyota Circular Factory is a new initiative that will curate what they call end-of-life vehicles (ELVs—junkers bound for the bone yard) and piece them out for repurposing, remanufacturing, and recycling. ELVs are vehicles tagged as hazardous waste, usually due to age or as the result of a crash.
According to the
European Union
, more than six million vehicles are left to rot, causing not only environmental issues but also an economic loss in the millions for the materials that can be repurposed. As such, the EU ELV Directive went into effect in 2000, with a regulation update proposed in 2023. The directive sets minimum requirements, which can be adapted for each member country.
The TCF program was established by Toyota Motor Europe (TME) and its name refers to all of TME’s recycling activities within the EU market. Globally, it’s the first operation of its kind within Toyota. The first location will be at Toyota Motor Manufacturing UK (TMUK)’s Burnaston plant, whose principal build is the Toyota Corolla.
Toyota Motor Europe
Through the TCF, each ELV will go through an extensive validation process before being sorted. Materials and parts will be tagged for three key areas: reusability for resale, refurbishing, and recycling. Reusable parts will be sold through Toyota retailers and parts distributors. Raw materials like copper, aluminum, steel, and plastic would be recycled and used in the production of new parts. Everything will be assessed, including commodities like batteries and wheels, on where their second life will begin.
“We initially anticipate recycling around 10,000 vehicles a year in our UK facility, which will give new life to 120,000 parts, recover 300 tons of high purity plastic and 8,200 tons of steel—amongst other materials,” said Leon van der Merwe, Vice President of Circular Economy at Toyota Motor Europe.
He added, “As a next step for the Toyota Circular Factory concept, we plan to roll out similar operations across Europe. And we’re not stopping at our own facilities – we are eager to collaborate with other organisations who share our passion of circularity and commitment to carbon neutrality.”
How does TMUK obtain these ELVs anyway? Per the
UK’s ELV regulations
, vehicles are registered but automakers also need to provide a take-back program free of charge. And there is an “unlimited fine” for non-compliance with ELVs.
This sounds more purposeful and just a better overall plan than, say,
Cash for Clunkers
. That federal program was done purely as an economic stimulus that resulted in thousands of vehicles being destroyed. Whereas in Toyota’s eyes, end of life really means a second chance.

data.title: An iPad dug up from the Thames solved museum thieves' murder plot
data.author: vinni2
data.article_summary: An iPad Mini found buried in the River Thames helped police uncover an international crime network involved in a murder plot. The iPad, discovered with a pink Vodafone SIM card, provided crucial call data linking three men to the attempted assassination of Paul Allen, a notorious armed robber. Allen survived a shooting in 2019, which left him paralysed. The investigation revealed the men, Louis Ahearne, Stewart Ahearne, and Daniel Kelly, had also committed a heist at a Swiss museum a month earlier, stealing Ming Dynasty artifacts worth £2.8 million. The crime spree included other incidents like a luxury apartment robbery. The meticulously planned assassination attempt involved surveillance and unregistered phones. The discovery of the iPad was pivotal in connecting these crimes and leading to the conviction of the three men.

How an iPad dug up from the Thames solved museum thieves' murder plot
18 hours ago
Share
Save
Thomas Mackintosh
BBC News, London
Share

Met Police
The iPad Mini was found buried one inch under the sand of the River Thames and linked to a near fatal shooting five-and-a-half years earlier
A Ming vase stolen from a Swiss museum. A shooting at a comedian's house in Woodford, east London. The robbery of a luxury apartment in Sevenoaks, Kent.
These seemingly unconnected events were all part of a web of international organised crime that police untangled after a six-year-long investigation.
A key piece of evidence - an iPad, found under an inch of sand on the foreshore of the River Thames just downstream from the O2 Arena.
Its discovery was pivotal to the investigation that has led to three people being found guilty at the Old Bailey of the near-assassination of one of Britain's most notorious armed robbers.
When found by a police officer with a metal detector on a cold November morning last year, the iPad was found caked in mud having been underwater for more than five years.
Forensics were able to clean it and open the Sim tray – which still contained a pink Vodafone Sim card.
Call data that was subsequently salvaged provided damning evidence on three men - Louis Ahearne, Stewart Ahearne and Daniel Kelly - who were all also involved in a heist at a museum in Switzerland a month earlier.
"I've questioned this a lot," Det Supt Matthew Webb ponders. "Is it calamitous blunders tripping them up or was it just they were so blasé they wouldn't get caught?"
A 'meticulously planned' assassination plot
Video doorbell footage captured audio of several gunshots
The Ahearne brothers and Kelly first caught the attention of police after gunshots pierced the silence of a late summer evening in an affluent Woodford area on 11 July 2019.
Six bullets tore through a glass conservatory at a luxury property owned by comedian Russell Kane that had been rented out to Paul Allen.
One severed one of Allen's fingers, the other went through his throat and became lodged in his spinal cord, leaving him struggling to breathe and bleeding profusely.
"He's been shot, he's been shot!" Allen's partner, Jade Bovington, screamed.
Met Police
Two bullets tore through the glass of a conservatory and hit Paul Allen as he stood inside his kitchen
As she frantically called an ambulance, neighbours and a private security guard heard the cries and rushed to render first aid.
One eyewitness described seeing an unidentified man vault a low wall, run between some bushes and get straight into a waiting vehicle which immediately sped off.
To this day, Allen relies on a wheelchair, paralysed below his upper chest.
Getty Images
Pictured in Morocco, Paul Allen was one of seven men who were jailed for their roles in the Securitas raid in February 2006
Allen gained notoriety as one of the ringleaders of what remains Britain's biggest ever armed robbery. In 2006, Allen was part of a balaclava-wearing gang toting guns including an AK-47 assault rifle who threatened to kill staff at the Securitas depot in Tonbridge, Kent. They
stole £53m in Bank of England cash notes
- leaving behind £154m which would not fit into their lorry.
Allen fled to Morocco four days later, but was arrested in Rabat alongside friend and fellow robber
Lee Murray
, who remains in jail in nearby Tiflet. In January 2008, Allen was extradited to the UK and subsequently sentenced to 18 years in prison.
Allen was released in 2016 and moved back to his roots in south-east London. But he relocated to Woodford with his partner and two younger children after a gunman opened fire at him and his pregnant daughter in the
doorway of their Woolwich home in September 2018
.
Ten months later, Allen almost died after those two bullets hit him as he stood in the kitchen of his Woodford haven.
Met Police
A bullet casing was found in the back garden of the property Paul Allen was living in when he was shot
Prosecutors argued the Ahearnes and Kelly were equally culpable in the plot to murder Allen - which involved a hired car, surveillance and unregistered pay-as-you-go phones.
"This was a meticulously researched and planned assassination attempt by a team of men well versed in the level of criminality to pull it off," prosecutor Michael Shaw KC said.
In discovering how the three knew where to find Allen, police would uncover their criminality stretched into mainland Europe.
The Geneva job and the Mayfair hotel sting
Just one month before the shooting, the Ahearne brothers and Kelly stood outside the Museum of Far Eastern Art in Geneva equipped with a sledgehammer, angle grinders and crowbars.
Within seconds of forcing their way through the front door, they shattered glass casings housing 14th Century Chinese Ming Dynasty antiques. Three items were seized - a rare pomegranate vase; a doucai-style wine cup and a porcelain bowl - and had a combined insured value of £2.8m.

data.article_summary:
本文讨论了自然数的公理化定义，旨在通过严格的数学框架来定义各种数，包括整数、有理数、实数和复数。文章首先指出自然数（如1, 2, 3等）常用于计数，但为了涵盖所有类型的数（如-4, √3, 22/7），需要一个精确的定义体系。文章介绍了佩亚诺公理（Peano Axioms），这是由意大利数学家朱塞佩·佩亚诺在1889年提出的，用于定义自然数。佩亚诺通过九条公理，其中四条涉及等号“=”的性质，另外五条则提供了自然数的完整定义。利用这些公理，可以推导出自然数的所有性质，并进一步构建整数、有理数、实数和复数系统。

文章还探讨了不依赖于计数概念来定义自然数的方法，提出通过集合论和“后继函数”S来描述自然数集{0, 1, 2, 3, ...}。该函数S将每个自然数映射到其下一个数，如S(0)=1, S(1)=2等，且S函数是单射但非满射。这种公理化方法仅依赖于最基本的性质，从而构建出一个严谨的数学体系。

不同观点：
• [parallel] 认为将Peano公理中的数字视为任意的无序标签（如单词"cat" "tree" "nut"等）能让这个练习显得更有意义，感觉像是在构建新事物，而不是将公理定义强加于已有的结构上。
• [NooneAtAll3] 指出Peano公理（Piano Axioms）与Peano算术（PA，一种常在公理讨论中出现的一阶公理系统）是不同的，并通过Goodstein序列的例子说明后者在某些数学命题（如Goodstein序列的终止）中的局限性。
• [082349872349872] 建议通过玩“自然数游戏”来熟悉这些公理，并提供了一个在线资源链接。
• [robertkoss] 表达了对数学公理（特别是ZFC和Peano公理）的浓厚兴趣，并提到Gödel不完备定理，强调了Peano公理在数学基础研究中的重要性。
• [culi] 对将Peano公理视为算术的唯一构建块表示不满，认为这只是众多尝试中的一种，旨在提出可以作为算术构建块的公理集合。

补充讨论：
• Peano公理与Peano算术的区别是讨论中的一个重要技术细节，[NooneAtAll3]通过引用Goodstein定理的例子强调了这一点。
• [culi] 提出了对Peano公理作为算术唯一基础的质疑，指出了数学中存在其他可能的公理体系，这一点引发了对Peano公理地位的争议。
• [parallel] 和 [robertkoss] 的观点展示了在数学教育和理解中，如何看待和使用Peano公理的不同视角。前者倾向于抽象化和概念化，而后者则对公理系统本身表现出浓厚兴趣。

争议焦点：
• Peano公理是否应被视为算术的唯一基础，还是只是众多公理体系中的一种。
• Peano公理与Peano算术的区别及其在数学证明中的应用范围。

An Axiomatic Study of Numbers
Introduction
Thinking of numbers intuitively brings to mind the simplest and most fundamental set of numbers, namely the
set of
natural numbers
. These numbers are used to count objects like cars, books, pens, etc. If we associate natural numbers such as
1, 2, 3,
etc. with counting, then with what corresponding concepts do we relate numbers like
-4, \sqrt{3} \text{ and } \frac{22}{7}
?
To reason about all kinds of numbers encountered during our study of mathematics, we need a precise mathematical framework for defining numbers. We will build this framework by first rigorously defining natural numbers axiomatically without relying on the intuitive notion of counting. Then, using this framework as a foundation, we will construct all the other sets of numbers such as integers, rational numbers, real numbers and complex numbers in terms of the natural numbers.
A good axiomatic system assumes as little as possible, while proving as much as possible. To create an efficient axiomatization for the natural numbers, we must distill these numbers to their essential properties. Intuitively, we understand various aspects of the natural numbers, such as their existence and the basic properties of the binary operations addition, multiplication, and the ‘less than’ relation. How few of these concepts can we take as axioms, from which we can deduce everything else that we need to know about the natural numbers? It turns out that remarkably little is required for the axiomatization of the natural numbers—neither addition, nor multiplication, nor the ‘less than’ relation need to be taken as axioms; these will all be constructed from our fundamental axioms.
The standard axiomatization of the natural numbers, know as the Peano Axioms, was originally formulated by the Italian mathematician, Giuseppe Peano. In
1889
, Peano developed the real number system based on his axioms for the natural numbers. He defined natural numbers through nine axioms, four of which established the properties of the equality relation “
=
” with regard to natural numbers, while the remaining five axioms provided a complete and rigorous definition of natural numbers.
In order to appreciate the intellectual feat of Peano, it’s worth noting that utilizing only his axioms, we are able to prove all the established properties of the natural numbers. Furthermore, these axioms facilitate the construction of the integer, rational, real, and complex number systems.
Before we discuss Peano’s Axioms in detail, it is a useful exercise to explore an alternative way to describe natural numbers, distinct from the usual intuitive notion of counting. Such an exploration would help us to independently arrive at Peano’s axioms.
Intuition behind the Axiomatic Definition of Natural Numbers
How do we model the concept of natural numbers denoted by
0, 1, 2, 3
and so on without relying on the notion of counting?

\{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\}
.
Let us denote the set of natural numbers as
\mathcal{N}
. First, we recognize that
0
should be a part of this set. Next, we want
0
to lead us to
1
,
1
to
2
and we should be able to continue this way, naming each successive number as far as we wish. This is illustrated below.
0 \rightarrow1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow \ldots
From the above diagram we can see that to model this relationship we need a “next” operation that given a natural number, produces the next natural number in the sequence.
The above diagram can also be viewed as shown below.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}

1 &\rightarrow 2 \\
2 &\rightarrow 3 \\
\vdots &\quad\,\,\,\, \vdots \\
\end{split}
\end{equation*}

S(0) = 1, S(1) = 2
and so forth. We will refer to this function
S
as the

data.title: What's Happening to Students?
data.author: atombender
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了当前学生因沉迷手机而导致学习能力下降的问题。教师们发现学生无法忍受无聊，总是依赖手机获取即时满足，表现为情绪化、缺乏长期目标，对学业和未来漠不关心。相比之下，监狱中的学生却表现出强烈的学习兴趣。文章还提到，儿童过早接触屏幕，尤其是在低收入家庭，导致他们入学时已成为“屏幕瘾者”。作者的研究显示，这种现象正以前所未有的速度恶化。此外，作弊现象在学生中十分普遍，达到40%的学生在一门伦理课上被发现作弊。文章呼吁关注技术对教育的负面影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对青少年沉迷互联网及屏幕时间过长的问题，以及技术和教育系统在其中的角色。

不同观点：
• Chromanoid 认为中国对青少年屏幕时间的限制是有益的，强调互联网和社交媒体需要受到严格管理，特别是对未成年人的影响。他提到现代互联网的诱惑远超过去，主张通过监管来保护孩子。
• Dmvdoug 则主张通过与学生沟通和倾听来解决问题，强调建立人际连接的重要性。他认为教育系统的僵化阻碍了这种方法的实施。
• Juunpp 持更激进的观点，主张直接禁止在学校使用手机，认为这是保证学生专注学习的唯一途径。
• Brianhama 对“指责技术”持怀疑态度，认为每个时代都有其“替罪羊”，如电话、摇滚音乐、电视等，现在的智能手机不过是新的对象。他并不为此感到担忧。
• Jmward01 将互联网和社交媒体比作“数字毒品”，强调需要认真对待并研究如何安全地将它们融入生活，类似于对待化学毒品的方式。
• Kurofune 将问题归因于社会和经济系统的破败，特别是年轻人无法购房的问题，认为这是导致缺乏动力的根本原因。
• Aeblyve 认为学生偏好互联网内容反映了教育系统的失败，主张反思教育与经济需求之间的关系。
• Ern 基于个人经历，认为屏幕本身不是问题，问题在于手机和社交媒体的特定功能，如通知和社交媒体的过度使用。
• Supportengineer 表达了对未来的悲观看法，认为当前社会问题在未来可能更加严重。
• Hoseja 批评教育系统是“空壳”，认为学生对系统的冷漠态度是一种反抗。
• Csomar 对学生的反叛行为持乐观态度，认为这是对过时教育系统的挑战，期待新一代能带来改变。
• Hibikir 认为互联网和新技术提供了更多学习工具，但也带来了更多诱惑，结果因人而异。
• Jmye 批评科技公司员工对公司负面影响的无视或辩护，认为他们应站出来反对不良实践。
• Siliconc0w 指出人工智能有潜力改善教育，但目前常被用于作弊，需要监管来确保技术发展的社会效益。
• OutOfHere 认为文章作者是为了保住自己的工作而夸大了问题，认为只有少数人需要“拯救”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应通过监管（如屏幕时间限制）来控制青少年使用互联网，还是应通过教育和沟通来解决问题。
• 技术在教育中的潜力和负面影响是另一个重要讨论点，特别是人工智能的应用和互联网的双重性（既是学习工具也是诱惑来源）。
• 社会和经济系统的结构性问题（如年轻人购房难）也被认为是影响学生动力的重要因素。
• 教育系统的僵化和过时被广泛批评，有人认为这是学生对学习失去兴趣的根本原因。

A frustrated teacher recently took to social media with a
desperate warning:
You guys don’t know what’s going on in education right now. That’s fine—how could you know unless you were working in it? But I think that you need to know….
First of all the kids have no ability to be bored whatsoever. They live on their phones. And they’re just fed a constant stream of dopamine from the minute their eyes wake up in the morning until they go to sleep at night.
Because they are in a constant state of dopamine withdrawal at school, they behave like addicts. They’re super emotional. The smallest things set them off.
When you are standing in front of them trying to teach, they’re vacant. They have no ability to tune in….
They’re not there.
And they have a level of apathy that I’ve never seen before in my whole career. Punishments don’t work because they don’t care about them. They don’t care about grades. They don’t care about college.
They just care about the next fix—because that’s how addicts operate. They have no long term plan, just short term needs.
They can’t get back to their phones fast enough.
Please support my work by taking out a premium subscription—for just $6 per month (even less if you sign up for a year).
Subscribe
How bad is it for educators right now?
Check out this commentary from one experienced teacher, who finds more engaged students in prison than a college classroom.
This comes from Corey McCall, a member of
The Honest Broker
community who recently
posted this comment
:
I saw this decline in both reading ability and interest occur firsthand between 2006 and 2021….I had experience teaching undergrads who hadn't comprehended the material before, but hadn't faced the challenge of students who could read it but who simply didn't care….
Since 2021 I've been teaching part-time in prison, and incarcerated students really want to learn. They love to read and think along with authors such as Plato, Descartes, and Simone de Beauvoir. I am teaching
Intro to Theater
this semester (the story of how this happened is interesting, but is irrelevant here) and students have been poring over
Oedipus the King
and asking why this amazing play isn't performed more regularly alongside plays like
Hamilton
and
The Lion King
.
I believe that there is hope for the humanities and perhaps for culture more generally, but it will be found in unusual places.
I’ve made a similar claim
in this article
—where I look outside of college for a rebirth of the humanities. It would be great if it happened in classrooms, too, but I fear that they are now the epicenter of the zombie wars.
Alas, I fear the number of zombie students is still growing—and at an accelerated pace.
Jonathan Haidt, who has taken the lead in exposing this crisis—and thus gets attacked fiercely by zombie apologists—shares horrifying trendlines from
Monitoring the Future
.
This group at the University of Michigan has studied student behavior since 1975. But what’s happening now is unprecedented.
Students are literally finding it
too hard to think
. So they can’t learn new things.
Source
Below are more ugly numbers from another in-depth study—which looks at how children spend their day.  It reveals that children
under the age of two
are already spending more than an hour per day on screens.
YouTube usage for this group has more than doubled in just four years.
Poor and marginalized communities are hurt the most. As your income drops, your children’s screen time more than doubles.
Source:
2025 study by Common Sense
In other words, these children are getting turned into screen addicts long before they enter the school system.
This is why teachers are speaking out. They see the fallout every day in their classrooms.
I’m dumbfounded when I hear ‘experts’ claim that phones are not the problem. Like  tobacco companies—whose hired experts long denied the connection between smoking and cancer—they say that “correlation does not prove causation.”
But that’s just sophistry and spin.
Parents, for example, have no doubts about the danger—because they see it happening right before their eyes.
Source:
2025 study by Common Sense
.
But let’s give tech companies some credit. They have improved one skill among current students—cheating, which has now reached epic proportions.
The situation is so extreme that more than 40% of students were caught cheating recently—
and it happened in an ethics class!
The professor caught them in a simple way. He simply uploaded a copy of his final exam on to the web, but with wrong answers.

• OutOfHere 认为文章作者是为了保住自己的工作而夸大了问题，认为只有少数人需要“拯救”。

• 争议焦点在于是否应通过监管（如屏幕时间限制）来控制青少年使用互联网，还是应通过教育和沟通来解决问题。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了由已故传奇人物dmr（Dennis M. Ritchie）编写的最早期的C语言编译器版本，这些版本目前无法使用现代编译器如gcc进行编译。发布这些代码仅供怀旧和纪念，它们代表了促成一个万亿美金行业的起点。要尝试运行这些编译器，可能需要使用Aiju提供的PDP-11/Unix模拟器。文章还提供了相关链接，包括PDP-11模拟器和Unix研究资源库，供有兴趣的人尝试。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [bluetomcat] 对C语言中"extern"和"auto"的使用方式进行了分析，指出其与现代C语言的不同，并提出了一些关于数组和变量类型的技术问题。
• [deweywsu] 和 [diginova] 讨论了自举（bootstrapping）的概念，即第一个C编译器是否用C语言编写，并提供了相关资料链接以帮助理解。
• [tempodox] 对早期C语言中`main(argc, argv)`的写法表示惊讶，并对PDP-11是否区分`char`和`int`提出了疑问。
• [robertkoss] 作为对低级语言不熟悉的人，询问了文件命名如"c01, c02"等的理由，寻求解释。
• [FeistySkink] 和 [smackay] 以幽默的方式参与讨论，前者开玩笑地建议项目应命名为"LegaC"，后者提到1972年作为与讨论相关的重要年份。
• [dark-star] 分享了一个名为"waste()"的函数，以幽默的方式展示了早期编程中的一些趣味代码片段，并暗示其影响了后来的Windows系统。

争议焦点：
• 对早期C语言的复杂性和简洁性的不同看法，[90s_dev] 对Zig语言的简洁性持怀疑态度，而 [ricardo81] 则强调了历史和技术积累的重要性。
• 对早期技术实现细节的讨论，如[bluetomcat] 和 [tempodox] 对C语言语法和使用方式的困惑和分析。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对自举编译器的技术探讨，[deweywsu] 和 [diginova] 提供了相关资料以帮助理解编译器如何用同一种语言编写。
• 对早期编程体验的怀旧和分享，[keyle] 和 [dark-star] 提到了早期操作系统和编程环境的体验，并表达了对某些设计风格的喜爱。

data.title: The surreal joy of having an overprovisioned homelab
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家庭服务器（homeserver）和家庭实验室（homelab）的配置、用途及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• [apexalpha] 支持使用K8s（Kubernetes）管理家庭服务器，认为手动管理整个技术栈非常有收获，并特别推荐Talos系统。这种做法可能涉及过度配置（over-provisioning），但学习效果显著。

• [WaxProlix] 偏好于使用低配置的旧系统（underprovisioned homelab），并从在有限硬件资源中榨取性能中获得满足感，例如在旧i3系统上运行更多容器和转码流。

• [1970-01-01] 提出未被讨论的电费问题，暗示高配置或长时间运行的服务器可能导致较高的能源成本。

• [QuiDortDine] 关注是否有人解决了机器人滥用问题，并对帖子中提到的解决方案表示兴趣，可能认为该方案对家庭服务器有实用价值。

• [keyle] 对开发者使用可爱图形（cutesie graphics）的现象提出疑问，表现出对这种风格或文化运动的困惑，并希望了解其起源和背景。

• [ipsento606] 对“家庭实验室”的定义和用途感到困惑，认为人们将家庭服务器称为“实验室”或“游乐场”并不准确，并主张家庭服务器应以功能性为主，而非纯粹的实验或娱乐用途。

补充讨论：
• 技术选择和配置（如K8s和Talos）带来的学习价值与硬件资源利用之间的平衡。
• 不同用户对硬件性能压榨的满足感与实际电费等运行成本之间的潜在矛盾。
• 对“家庭实验室”和“家庭服务器”这两个术语的定义和使用存在理解差异，部分用户强调功能性，而其他用户则关注实验性和娱乐性。

争议焦点：家庭服务器和家庭实验室的定义与用途存在分歧，部分用户认为它是功能性设备，而另一些用户则视其为技术实验和娱乐的平台。

data.title: Rest Easy
data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了“休息”的概念，从俄国作家冈察洛夫的小说《奥勃洛莫夫》中的主人公对休息的看法谈起。奥勃洛莫夫认为生活的目的就是终日无所事事地躺在床上休息。文章进一步讨论了“休息”的定义，指出它不同于睡眠、 leisure（闲暇）或懒惰。作者以个人经验说明随着年龄增长，休息和睡眠变得愈发复杂和不易。文章还提到《圣经》中上帝创世后休息的例子，以及不同宗教对神圣休息日的重视，如犹太教的安息日和基督教的星期日礼拜。最后，文章指出，休息对恶人是无缘的，地狱之所以可怕部分正是因为没有休息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章的不同角度的看法与反馈，涉及睡眠的重要性、文章本身的质量以及技术工具需求等

补充讨论：
• [jalk] 并未直接讨论文章主题，而是询问是否有简单的命令行工具用于调用REST端点，与文章内容无直接关系。

• [hyfgfh] 发表了一句简短的评论 "no rest for the wicked"，可能是一种文字游戏，未对文章内容进行具体讨论。

争议焦点：

- 睡眠时间减少对健康的影响存在不同看法，[aredox] 强调睡眠不足的危害。

43450745.article_content:
The Russian novelist Ivan Goncharov once said of writers, “And to write and write, like a wheel or a machine, tomorrow, the day after, on holidays; summer will come—and he must still be writing. When is he to stop and rest? Unfortunate man?” Goncharov was born in 1812 and died in 1891, so I am clearly not the model for the writer he was talking about—even though, my prolificacy having often been commented upon, I could otherwise well be. The eponymous hero of his novel
Oblomov
feels the same way about another character in the book who loves travel, and a second one who enjoys a lively social life, and a third who works hard in the hope of promotion. All of them are viewed by Oblomov as absurdly out of synch with life’s real purpose. This purpose, as Oblomov sees it, is to lie abed doing nothing all the days of one’s life. If
rest
may be said to have a champion, it is Oblomov, a gentleman by birth for whom “life was divided, in his opinion, into two halves: one consisted of work and boredom—these words were for him synonymous—the other of rest and peaceful good-humor.” Rest, unrelenting rest, is the name of Oblomov’s game.
“Just as there are polysyllabic words that say very little,” Georg Christoph Lichtenberg wrote, “so there are also monosyllabic words of infinite meaning.” “Rest” is one of those words, simple-sounding yet not easily defined. As a verb, rest means to “cease work or movement in order to relax, refresh oneself, or recover strength”; as a noun, “an instance or period of relaxing or ceasing to engage in strenuous or stressful activity.” Why isn’t this very helpful?
Rest is not quite synonymous with sleep, leisure, or laziness. When a man in his mid-70s or older asks another man of roughly the same age if he is “getting much,” he probably isn’t referring to sex but to sleep. Like as not, neither man is getting much sleep, for few older men I know make it through the night without having to get up two, three, or more times. Some are compelled to do so to visit the House of Commons, as Dylan Thomas called the bathroom. Others find their minds racing, or their sleep invaded by goofy dreams. I had a friend, a contemporary, who suffered the trifecta of insomnia, megalomania, and paranoia, and so spent the better parts of his nights awake, worrying about losing power he didn’t really have.
As an adolescent, I remember sleeping eight-, nine-, 10-hour periods. Now if I can do two or three hours at a stretch, I feel vaguely triumphant. Conversations with friends, though they bring much pleasure, tend toward the stimulating and so do not necessarily qualify as rest. Working out of my apartment, as I have for many years now, I often take afternoon naps, but these naps do not so much bring on a restful feeling as they ward off the inevitable fatigue of a man in his 80s.
Twenty-five years ago, I wrote an essay called “The Art of the Nap,” in which I set out my prowess at the act. What I remember about the essay today is an anecdote involving Hugh Lloyd-Jones, then regius professor of Greek at Oxford (because he was still alive, I didn’t use his name). Lloyd-Jones seemed to me in those days an Englishman to the highest power: He seemed to have 50 or 60 teeth, Himalayas of dandruff covered the shoulders of his blue blazer, and he spoke with a slight Oxbridge stammer. When I asked him if he napped, he replied, “Whenever possible.” Supine or prone? “Supine.” On couch or bed? “Bed.” Trousers on or off? “Generally off.” And for how long? “That depends,” he answered, “on when the cats get up.”
_____________
The concept of rest is as old as the Bible
.
On the seventh day, after creating the world and all that was in it, we are told that the Lord rested. Not, however, in His case, from fatigue, but to contemplate His further creations. Alain Corbin, a French scholar who has recently published a brief
History of Rest,
holds that for God, the day of rest was “a creative pause.” Later on, God tells Moses: “Speak to the sons of Israel and say, ‘You must keep my sabbaths carefully, because the sabbath is a
sign between myself and you
from generation to generation to show that it is I who sanctify you. You must keep the sabbath, then; it is to be held sacred by you.’”
Keeping the Sabbath, in Corbin’s words, is not about rest alone but “the holy nature of that rest.”
Mutatis mutandis,
Christians, who were of course initially mostly Jews, took up the notion of a holy day of rest, with theirs being Sunday. In some quarters, both religions are even now defined by their days of rest. Militant Islamists have been known to claim that “after we finish off the Saturday people, we shall finish you, the Sunday people.” Meanwhile, it is understood that there is no rest for the wicked, which is to say none in Hell, which in good part is what must make it so hellish.

data.author: _tk_
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在2024年3月15日美国轰炸也门胡塞武装目标前两小时，通过Signal加密消息应用收到时任国防部长Pete Hegseth发送的作战计划。文章追溯到2023年10月哈马斯入侵以色列南部后，受伊朗支持的胡塞武装对以色列和国际航运发动袭击，扰乱全球贸易。拜登政府未能有效反击，而即将上任的特朗普政府则承诺更强硬回应。作者收到自称为特朗普国家安全顾问Michael Waltz的联系请求，随后被加入一个讨论胡塞武装的Signal群组，该群组包括多名自称是美国高级安全官员的人。尽管作者对群组真实性存疑，但最终通过该群组提前得知了即将发生的军事行动。

using AI narration. Listen to more stories on the Noa app.
The world found out shortly before 2 p.m. eastern time on March 15 that the United States was bombing Houthi targets across Yemen.
I, however, knew two hours before the first bombs exploded that the attack might be coming. The reason I knew this is that
Pete Hegseth
, the secretary of defense, had texted me the war plan at 11:44 a.m. The plan included precise information about weapons packages, targets, and timing.
This is going to require some explaining.
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter.
Sign up for it here.
The story technically begins shortly after the Hamas invasion of southern Israel, in October 2023. The Houthis—an Iran-backed terrorist organization whose motto is “God is great, death to America, death to Israel, curse on the Jews, victory to Islam”—soon launched attacks on Israel and on international shipping, creating havoc for global trade. Throughout 2024, the Biden administration was ineffective in countering these Houthi attacks; the incoming Trump administration promised a tougher response.
This is where Pete Hegseth and I come in.
On Tuesday, March 11, I received a connection request on Signal from a user identified as Michael Waltz. Signal is an open-source encrypted messaging service popular with journalists and others who seek more privacy than other text-messaging services are capable of delivering. I assumed that the Michael Waltz in question was President Donald Trump’s national security adviser. I did not assume, however, that the request was from the actual Michael Waltz. I have met him in the past, and though I didn’t find it particularly strange that he might be reaching out to me, I did think it somewhat unusual, given the Trump administration’s contentious relationship with journalists—and Trump’s periodic fixation on me specifically. It immediately crossed my mind that someone could be masquerading as Waltz in order to somehow entrap me. It is not at all uncommon these days for nefarious actors to try to induce journalists to share information that could be used against them.
I accepted the connection request, hoping that this was the actual national security adviser, and that he wanted to chat about Ukraine, or Iran, or some other important matter.
Two days later—Thursday—at 4:28 p.m., I received a notice that I was to be included in a Signal chat group. It was called the “Houthi PC small group.”
A message to the group, from “Michael Waltz,” read as follows: “Team – establishing a principles [
sic
] group for coordination on Houthis, particularly for over the next 72 hours. My deputy Alex Wong is pulling together a tiger team at deputies/agency Chief of Staff level following up from the meeting in the Sit Room this morning for action items and will be sending that out later this evening.”
The message continued, “Pls provide the best staff POC from your team for us to coordinate with over the next couple days and over the weekend. Thx.”
The term
principals committee
generally refers to a group of the senior-most national-security officials, including the secretaries of defense, state, and the treasury, as well as the director of the CIA. It should go without saying—but I’ll say it anyway—that I have never been invited to a White House principals-committee meeting, and that, in my many years of reporting on national-security matters, I had never heard of one being convened over a commercial messaging app.
One minute later, a person identified only as “MAR”—the secretary of state is
Marco Antonio Rubio
—wrote, “Mike Needham for State,” apparently designating the current counselor of the State Department as his representative. At that same moment, a Signal user identified as “
JD Vance
” wrote, “Andy baker for VP.” One minute after that, “TG” (presumably
Tulsi Gabbard
, the director of national intelligence, or someone masquerading as her) wrote, “Joe Kent for DNI.” Nine minutes later, “Scott B”—apparently Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, or someone spoofing his identity, wrote, “Dan Katz for Treasury.” At 4:53 p.m., a user called “Pete Hegseth” wrote, “Dan Caldwell for DoD.” And at 6:34 p.m., “Brian” wrote “Brian McCormack for NSC.” One more person responded: “John Ratcliffe” wrote at 5:24 p.m. with the name of a CIA official to be included in the group. I am not publishing that name, because that person is an active intelligence officer.
The principals had apparently assembled. In all, 18 individuals were listed as members of this group, including various National Security Council officials; Steve Witkoff, President Trump’s Middle East and Ukraine negotiator; Susie Wiles, the White House chief of staff; and someone identified only as “S M,” which I took to stand for
Stephen Miller
. I appeared on my own screen only as “JG.”
That was the end of the Thursday text chain.

data.author: anta40
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：适用于不同架构（如ARM、RISC-V）的非传统或小众操作系统

不同观点：
• [pajko] 提到了多个操作系统，包括Haiku、AROS、MorphOS、AmigaOS 4、Inferno、Illumos，涵盖了多种架构和历史背景，但没有深入讨论具体特性。
• [dlcarrier] 补充了RISC OS，强调其历史背景（为Acorn电脑开发）以及其轻量级但功能齐全的特点，包括GUI和网络功能。
• [andsoitis] 详细介绍了Inferno，引用官方描述并强调其分布式特性和与Plan 9的关系。
• [wormius] 提到了Plan 9的一个分支9front，并提供了安装介质的详细信息，特别指出了支持的硬件如Raspberry Pi和QEMU。
• [mepian] 提到了MIT Lisp机器系统和Mezzano，后者是一个较新的用Common Lisp编写的操作系统，运行在ARM架构上。
• [snvzz] 提到了Niklaus Wirth的Oberon系统，提供了一个项目链接。
• [slicktux] 提到了XINU操作系统，并推荐了一本关于操作系统设计的书。
• [lboc] 提出是否需要实际硬件支持，并提到了一些模拟器如VM370。
• [mappu] 详细列举了多个操作系统及其对ARM和RISC-V的支持情况，包括ToaruOS、SerenityOS、Haiku、ReactOS和Skift。
• [yann-gael] 提到了MorphOS和AROS，特别指出它们可以将旧Mac电脑转变为类似Amiga的系统。
• [evanjrowley] 提到了Redox-OS，并指出其在Raspberry Pi 3 B+上的支持情况，同时提到其DOS模拟器和Cosmic桌面环境。
• [raggi] 简单提到了Fuchsia OS。
• [vandyswa] 提到了RSX-280，强调其与DOS和UNIX的不同。
• [Amlal] 补充了Haiku OS，分享了个人使用体验并对比了Linux和OS X。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点似乎在于哪些操作系统可以真正运行在实际硬件上，以及对不同架构（如ARM、RISC-V）的支持程度。
• 多个评论提到了模拟器和虚拟机的使用，这表明在讨论中模拟环境被视为一种可行的解决方案。
• 个人使用体验和历史背景的分享为讨论增加了一些实用性和趣味性，如[Amlal]对Haiku OS的评价。

总结：
讨论涵盖了多个小众操作系统，重点在于它们对不同硬件架构的支持情况和历史背景。参与者们提供了丰富的链接和个人见解，使得讨论更加全面和深入。

43477947.article_content:
mar 25
OpenSMTPD & Maildrop working in concert
OpenBSD has many ways of filtering mails based on criteria right out of the
box. But sometimes, the workload you want to put on your incoming mail is
better suited for tools designed just for that.
Long ago, procmail dominated this space. But since the projectâs last commit
was September 10th, 2001, itâs better to reach for tools that are still
active.
Maildrop
The
Courier Mail Server
comes with
many programs, and thankfully, if you already have an
MTA
that you lean on
but still wanted to use some of their fancy tooling, that will be fine.
In our case, we wanted to use
maildrop(1)
, which when installed on OpenBSD,
comes with a handful of filtering options, the Mail Delivery Agent (
MDA
),
some
MIME
building programs, etc. Installing is as follows:
# pkg_add maildrop # N.B. the non-postfix package will do
We like to use maildrop(5) in âdeliveryâ mode, whereby the
MDA
listens on
a socket, and you can start, stop, restart it like any other service. You can
play with maildrop(5) in manual mode, or the third option: embedded mode.
What we really liked about this project was how opinionated it was, how well
the documentation was crafted, and how packed the
mailing list
was with years of
helpful solutions.
However, little was out there in the form of a quick and dirty guide to
get everything humming along. Which, to be honest, has become a modern-day
pattern for how to do things. Furthermore,
AI
chatbots were very unhelpful
and hallucinated more than normal.
Light configuration
Because maildrop(5) is so opinionated, the following configuration are not
just suggestions, they are the rule (for the most part). If a certain
permission isnât just so, maildrop(5) wonât run. This is for security reasons,
and we can really get behind that.
In âdeliveryâ mode, your regular user needs a â~/.mailfilterâ file with â0600â permissions.
The naming is not mutable, at least out of the box. Also, this file needs to be owned by said user.
This is the âfilterâ for your mail, and it can be very complex. It can perform
things as trite as a âvacation reply,â to do email munging â like what we are
up to over at
Whenhen.com
. The
maildropfilter(7)
is a whole Turing-complete language, so be confident that it will meet your every
need.
Here is a plain-jane â.mailfilterâ configuration that just matches on a âFromâ
email, and based on that, files it into a Maildir directory found in the home
directory named â.vipâ :
if (/^From:.*vip@foo.com/)
{
to .vip
}
Here, maildrop(5) again will complain loudly if this â.vipâ isnât
a
bone fide
Maildrop directory. So set it up as it expects as
follows:
cd ~
mkdir -p .vip/{cur,new,tmp}
While weâre at it, create your regular Maildir (for all other mail) in
your home directory named â.maildirâ as well.
mkdir -p .maildir/{cur,new,tmp}
When maildir(5) is running in âdeliveryâ mode, the option to debug has
to be set up via the system config file, â/etc/courier/authdaemonrcâ.
While a â-V Kâ flag is available for the other modes, it isnât a valid
one in âdeliveryâ mode. Ergo the ârcâ file. This file is also strictly
a â0600â file with âroot:wheelâ ownership.
You can make your debugging as chatty as youâd like with this ârcâ file,
or, like us, you can test things in âmanualâ mode till everything is
working smoothly. In âdeliveryâ mode, with debugging on, you can follow
the messages with the usual
tail -f /var/log/messages
.
Preparing the daemon
The maildrop(5) daemon is called âauthdaemondâ and lives in
â/usr/local/sbinâ. Yes, itâs named âDaemon Daemon.â Thereâs a first
for everything!
It runs as root, and writes a âpidâ file to â/var/run/courier-authâ, so
better make this directory before you forget and maildrop(5) complains
about it:
# mkdir /var/run/courier-auth
This can be tweaked in your â/etc/courier/authdaemonrcâ file, but
thereâs nothing wrong with the default.
Lastly, a dirty solution to start the daemon at startup can be achieved
by prepending a line to rootâs crontab(1), as follows:
@reboot /bin/sh /usr/local/sbin/authdaemond start
...
Some interesting information is available from the install âREADMEâ
here
.
SMTPD
configuration
Thankfully, the OpenBSD folks have made working with your custom
MDA
s painless. Thereâs a first class way of going about it.
For example:
...
action "vip" mda "/usr/local/bin/maildrop -d %{dest.user:lowercase}"
match from any mail-from "vip@foo.com" for any action "vip"
...
This set up a rule that mail coming from a certain someone, will
get handled by maildrop(5). Itâs even a tad redundant, having a
filter, before a filter, but itâs up to you how you want to decide
what gets sent to â.maildirâ, what gets sent to maildrop(5), etc.
Here is a fleshed-out example that
sends local mail to â/var/mail/userâ, all Internet mail to

data.title: CIA Director Reveals Signal Comes Installed on Agency Computers
data.author: jbegley
data.article_summary: 在美国参议院情报委员会2025年3月25日的听证会上，CIA局长约翰·拉特克利夫透露，Signal这款端到端加密通讯应用已被政府高层采用，甚至预装在CIA电脑上。这一表态与FBI多年来对加密通讯的批评形成鲜明对比。FBI曾指责此类应用被犯罪分子和恐怖分子利用，威胁国家安全，并主张建立后门以监控通讯。然而，随着“Salt Typhoon”黑客事件曝光，未加密通讯的脆弱性显露无遗，政府机构开始推荐使用Signal等加密应用防范外国黑客。尽管FBI仍主张“负责任管理”的加密后门方案，CIA已公开采用Signal，显示出对其安全和隐私价值的认可。这一举动引发了对政府透明度和记录保存的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Signal在美情报界使用的合理性、合规性及安全性

不同观点：
• [jandrewrogers] 认为，Signal在美情报界被广泛使用，尤其是在非保密通信中替代了Gmail。他指出，Signal多年前就被美情报界认可，用于非保密甚至部分保密通信。这种使用并不是价值判断，而是现实情况。

• [colmmacc] 对Signal的合规性提出质疑，指出Signal缺乏FIPS验证和FedRamp认证，且其核心加密技术不符合NIST标准。这暗示了Signal在联邦政府使用中可能面临合规问题。

• [epistasis] 强调Signal只能用于安排会议等非保密用途，不能传输如战争计划等秘密材料，否则相关人员应承担后果。这表明对Signal在处理敏感信息方面的限制和责任追究。

• [lenerdenator] 质疑Signal是否被用于发送真正敏感的信息，并提出是否只有不称职的人才会这样做，暗示对Signal在敏感信息传输中的可靠性和适用性的怀疑。

• [jaysonelliot] 提出法律合规问题，质疑CIA是否不受《联邦记录法》约束，或者是否在无视法律。这涉及Signal使用中的法律和政策问题。

• [bediger4000] 认为这可能只是对Goldberg聊天事件的损害控制，暗示对Signal使用的讨论可能是为了应对特定事件的公关处理。

• [raggi] 仅简单提到“dedramp”，可能是在暗示减少或取消对Signal的使用，但没有进一步解释。

43478091.article_content:
FBI Director Kash Patel, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, and CIA Director John Ratcliffe at a Senate Committee on Intelligence hearing on March 25, 2025, in Washington, D.C.
Photo: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images
For years, U.S.
officials villainized end-to-end encrypted messaging apps like Signal as the domain of criminals and terrorists and a threat to national security.
As fallout over a Signal group chat about Yemen war plans ricocheted through Washington, however, CIA Director John Ratcliffe revealed at a Senate Intelligence Committee hearing on Tuesday that the app is approved for official communication and even comes installed on agency computers.
One longtime critic of government attacks on secure messaging said it was a sign that everybody else should follow suit.
“For everyday Americans, this seems like an inadvertent but strong endorsement of the cybersecurity and privacy value that Signal represents — assuming you actually know who you’re adding to the given chats,” said Sean Vitka, executive director of the progressive group Demand Progress.
“Going Dark”
The highly sensitive discussion over whether and when to attack Houthis in Yemen included two members of the panel at Tuesday’s hearing, according to a blockbuster
report
Monday from The Atlantic’s Jeffrey Goldberg.
There was particular irony to an FBI director’s presence on the panel next to members of the thread. For years, successive FBI chiefs Chris Wray and James Comey had
lambasted
end-to-end
encryption
. The FBI
popularized
the idea that terrorists and drug cartels were “
going dark
” on law enforcement, and that the government needed to step in to do something about it.
The FBI’s
favored solution
was to create a back door in the apps that would allow the government to snoop on conversations — but only with proper authority, the FBI said.
In a 2014 speech, then-FBI Director Comey
said
that the “post-Snowden pendulum has swung too far” in favor of privacy. Without creating a back door, he added, “homicide cases could be stalled, suspects could walk free, and child exploitation victims might not be identified or recovered.”
The FBI never made much progress in Congress toward securing a back door. Across the pond, attacks on end-to-end encryption are ongoing, with the United Kingdom reportedly ordering Apple in secret to create one. France’s National Assembly last week
voted down a backdoor mandate
sought by the country’s Interior Ministry.

Victims of UCLA Mob Attack Sue to “Hold the Aggressors Accountable”
Jonah Valdez, Akela Lacy
Texas’s GOP Governor Can Arbitrarily Deny Democrats a Seat in Congress Until Next Year

The CIA Seal of Approval
The FBI’s official position became increasingly tenuous last year when revelations about “Salt Typhoon” hackers made clear that unencrypted communications were highly vulnerable to foreign adversaries.
Related
How to Protect Yourself From the Salt Typhoon Hack, No Matter What the FBI Says
The hackers, who were allegedly affiliated with the Chinese government, targeted phones used by Donald Trump, JD Vance, and the Kamala Harris campaign, according to reports, and in some cases were able to scoop up the content of text conversations.
By December, the FBI was still promoting back doors under the banner of what it calls “responsibly managed” encryption. At the same time, however, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency was advising end-to-end encrypted messaging apps such as Signal as a defense against Chinese hackers.
Signal
, which is based on an open-source protocol and operated by a nonprofit foundation, is
designed to reduce to a minimum
the amount of information that the app can access. Only the users involved in a conversation have decryption keys, making it impossible for the Signal Foundation to view unencrypted conversations. The foundation also cannot see metadata such as a user’s contacts.
On Tuesday, Ratcliffe revealed that the government has adopted Signal at the highest echelons.
“One of the first things that happened when I was confirmed as CIA director was Signal was loaded onto my computer at the CIA.”
“One of the first things that happened when I was confirmed as CIA director was Signal was loaded onto my computer at the CIA, as it is for most CIA officers,” Ratcliffe said.
The practice began during President Joe Biden’s administration and had the official approval of CIA records management officials, Ratcliffe said, as long as “any decisions that are made are also recorded through formal channels.”
Critics of government secrecy were immediately alarmed that government officials might be trying to evade leaving records subject to the Freedom of Information Act or the
Presidential Records Act
by using private devices with disappearing messages.

43478525.article_content:
CxO
89
2 in 5 techies quit over inflexible workplace policies
89
Return to office, hours and intensity of work cited as reasons to walk
Paul Kunert
Mon 24 Mar 2025
//
12:33 UTC
Two in five techies quit in the past year because their employer didn't offer requisite flexibility with respect to hours, location and the "intensity of work."
The findings come from a survey of 26,000 plus staff that operate in 35 markets, including 2,548 respondents in tech, and fly in the face of more and more corporations issuing return to office mandates and demanding long working hours.
Vodafone: Be in the office 8 days a month or lose bonuses
READ MORE
Amsterdam-based recruitment biz Randstad, which commissioned the research, says 40 percent of the tech people it polled said they resigned due to hardline policies, and 56 percent threatened to seek an alternative if their requests for flexibility were ignored.
Almost three-quarters claim remote work boosts a "sense of community" with colleagues – versus the average of 58 percent across other sectors – and 68 percent say they'd trust their employer more if they were more easy going on hours, the intensity of the work and the place where they can work.
Graig Paglieri, Randstad Digital boss, said the "IT sector has shown that personalized work benefits and flexible options are essential not only for attracting top talent but also for retaining them in competitive markets. Policies should align with organizational, team and individual needs, ensuring a flexible and tailored approach."
In a separate survey of 1,060 recruiters across 21 markets, some employers seem to be acknowledging requests for flexibility. More than a third say businesses now accommodate different working arrangements and introduced policies related to this in the past year, while 81 percent think this helps create equity at work.
The sentiments reflect the findings from Pew Research's American Trends Panel in January, where nearly a half of the 5,395 randomly selected US adults said they'd
walk if their bosses told them they could no longer work from home
.
Not all tech bosses are listening to their staff, however.
Amazon
, Meta,
Google
, Elon Musk's collection of businesses,
IBM
,
Dell
, and many others are demanding staff come back into the office.
'Return to Office' declared dead
HR expert says biz leaders scared RTO mandates lead to staff attrition
Hybrid working? Buckle in, there's no turning back as survey takers insist: You can't make us go back
91% of polled Amazon staff unhappy with return-to-office, 3-in-4 want to jump ship
Reasons given for the shift in the post-pandemic policy to return-to-the-office include better innovation from in-person work, helping younger staff to learn the culture and the job better, and improving productivity.
It all depends in which field of tech someone operates – there is little point, for example, in a software engineer being asked to work on site. There are, however, studies that show
productivity does not take a hit
from home working, no matter how
paranoid
the bosses can be.
As for the demand from Google co-founder Sergei Brin to work
60 hours weeks
, with at least five of them in the office… the less said about that, the better. ®

data.author: hndecision1234

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：成年人是否应该回学校深造，特别是在工程或计算机科学等技术领域，以及回学校所需的时间、金钱和精力是否值得。

不同观点：
• **支持回学校深造**：
  - **sircastor**：分享了自己37岁回学校，40岁获得学位的经历，认为教育是值得的目标，鼓励根据个人情况做出决定，尤其是如果有经济支持（如教会学校补贴）或工作单位提供学费支持。
  - **dahart**：鼓励尝试回学校，指出可以通过贷款、奖学金、雇主资助等方式减轻经济压力，同时强调学位对职业转换的长远好处。
  - **cableshaft**：分享了自己28岁回学校完成计算机科学学位的经验，认为尽管年龄差距存在，但适应后一切正常，且有助于职业发展。

• **反对或质疑回学校深造**：
  - **an_aparallel**：基于自己的经历，批评成人教育的质量问题，包括教师水平、课程外包等，认为除非去顶尖学校，否则不值得。
  - **SoftTalker**：认为作为成年人回学校不值得，尤其是要和年轻人一起上课，建议通过在线课程或自学提升技能，因为学位在职业后期并不那么重要。
  - **bitbasher**：质疑回学校的必要性，尤其是已经在软件开发领域工作的人，认为高成本和时间投入不划算。

• **中立或具体建议**：
  - **lizknope**：建议先明确想学的具体专业和原因，并研究学校的课程设置，特别是美国社区大学和公立大学的合作项目，可以节省成本。
  - **programmertote**：建议先尝试一些相关课程，再决定是否完全投入机械或电气工程的学习，因为实际学习可能与理想中的不一样。
  - **xupybd**：介绍能力本位教育（CBE），可以通过展示已有知识缩短学习时间。
  - **gcanyon**：建议与目标大学的招生团队沟通，获取转学和课程选择的建议，以减少转学过程中的麻烦。
  - **mettamage**：推荐了几个欧洲和美国的在线学位项目，如德克萨斯大学和赫尔辛基大学的项目，认为这些项目在费用和质量上具有优势。
  - **csantini**：推荐欧洲的学位项目，特别是德国、意大利、法国等国家的免费或低成本英语授课项目，认为这些项目的教育质量高且费用低。

• **其他路径**：
  - **gpnt**：提出自学并通过考试获得学位的风险路径，认为目前缺乏为自学者设计的教育项目，但可以通过与大学协商使用实验室和课程资源。

补充讨论：
- **经济和时间成本**：多位评论者提到回学校的经济负担和时间投入，尤其是对有家庭和全职工作的人来说，这是一大挑战。
- **职业发展**：一些人认为学位对职业转换或晋升有帮助，但也有观点指出在技术领域，实际技能和工作经验比学位更重要。
- **教育质量**：一些评论者对成人教育的质量提出质疑，特别是教师水平和课程外包问题，建议选择学校时要谨慎。
- **欧洲的教育机会**：几位评论者提到欧洲的免费或低成本学位项目，认为这些项目是值得考虑的替代方案。

争议焦点：回学校深造的价值和可行性，特别是在成年阶段，是否值得投入大量时间和金钱，以及是否有更好的自学或在线学习途径。
